```tsx
  Link: ({ href, children, onPress }: { href: string; children: ReactElement; onPress?: unknown }) => cloneElement(children, { href, onPress } as object),
  Redirect: () => null,
  Stack: () => null,
  router: { push: () => undefined, replace: () => undefined, back: () => undefined, canGoBack: () => false },
  useLocalSearchParams: () => shell.params,
  usePathname: () => shell.pathname,
}));
vi.mock("@/lib/session", () => ({ useSession: () => ({ state: shell.state, refresh: async () => shell.state }) }));
// A post card's images reach native modules that do not load in Node; no image is drawn here.
vi.mock("expo-image", () => ({ Image: () => null }));
// The layout comes from the window's width, which a static render does not have: the test names the kind.
vi.mock("@/theme/layout", async (importOriginal) => ({ ...(await importOriginal<object>()), useLayout: () => shell.kind }));
// The title goes into the document's head through expo-router/head; here it is drawn in place, so a test can read it.
vi.mock("expo-router/head", () => ({ default: ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => createElement("template", { "data-head": "" }, children) }));

/** The fake toaster: sonner's custom toasts and dismissals are recorded, and its Toaster keeps the props it was given. */
const sonner = vi.hoisted(() => ({ custom: vi.fn(), dismiss: vi.fn(), props: [] as Record<string, unknown>[] }));
vi.mock("sonner", async () => {
  const { createElement: element } = await import("react");
  return {
    toast: Object.assign(vi.fn(), { custom: sonner.custom, dismiss: sonner.dismiss }),
    Toaster: (props: Record<string, unknown>) => {
      sonner.props.push(props);
      return element("section", { "data-fake-toaster": "" });
    },
  };
});

const html = (element: ReactElement): string => renderToStaticMarkup(element);
/** The markup's text as a reader sees it: tags dropped, spaces collapsed. */
const textOf = (markup: string): string => markup.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ").replace(/&#x27;/g, "'").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
/** The part of the markup inside the first element whose opening tag matches `open`, up to its closing tag of the same name. */
function inside(markup: string, open: RegExp): string {
  const found = open.exec(markup);
  if (!found) return "";
  const tag = /^<([a-z0-9]+)/.exec(found[0])![1]!;
  let depth = 0;
  const pattern = new RegExp(`<(/?)${tag}(?=[ >])[^>]*>`, "g");
  pattern.lastIndex = found.index;
  for (let match = pattern.exec(markup); match; match = pattern.exec(markup)) {
    depth += match[1] ? -1 : 1;
    if (depth === 0) return markup.slice(found.index, match.index + match[0].length);
  }
  return markup.slice(found.index);
}
/** Every anchor's opening tag. */
const anchors = (markup: string): string[] => markup.match(/<a\b[^>]*>/g) ?? [];
const hrefOf = (tag: string): string => /href="([^"]*)"/.exec(tag)?.[1] ?? "";

const ME = { user: { id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001", onboarded: true }, profile: { handle: "ada" }, standing: null } as unknown as MeResponse;
const signedIn = () => ({ status: "signed-in", me: ME });

afterEach(() => {
  shell.pathname = "/";
  shell.state = { status: "signed-out" };
  shell.kind = "phone";
  shell.params = {};
  vi.mocked(useReducedMotion).mockReturnValue(false);
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
  setComposeButtonShown(false);
});

const KINDS: LayoutKind[] = ["phone", "tablet", "desktop", "wide"];

describe("the navigation (sections 7.1 to 7.3)", () => {
  // 2d (decision 24, 10.1): Activity second; the phone's tab bar keeps four items and reaches Settings from the profile.
  const SIGNED_IN_ITEMS: Record<LayoutKind, string[]> = {
    phone: ["/", "/activity", "/bookmarks", "/u/ada"],
    tablet: ["/", "/activity", "/bookmarks", "/u/ada", "/settings"],
    desktop: ["/", "/activity", "/bookmarks", "/u/ada", "/settings"],
    wide: ["/", "/activity", "/bookmarks", "/u/ada", "/settings"],
  };

  test("at every layout the nav is a landmark named Main whose items are real anchors, in today's order and hrefs, with one current item", () => {
    for (const kind of KINDS) {
      shell.kind = kind;
      shell.state = signedIn();
      shell.pathname = "/bookmarks";
      const out = html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>);
      expect(out, kind).toContain(`data-layout="${kind}"`);
      const nav = inside(out, /<nav\b[^>]*aria-label="Main"[^>]*>/);
      expect(nav, kind).not.toBe("");
      expect(anchors(nav).map(hrefOf), kind).toEqual(SIGNED_IN_ITEMS[kind]);
      const current = anchors(nav).filter((tag) => tag.includes('aria-current="page"'));
      expect(current, kind).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(current[0], kind).toContain('href="/bookmarks"');
      // The current item's icon is drawn at the strong stroke, a shape cue beside its colour; the others at the usual one.
      // (Its pill and bar are classes, which a static render does not draw: the browser check measures them.)
      const items = nav.split(/(?=<a\b)/).slice(1);
      expect(items.filter((item) => item.includes('stroke-width="2.25"')).map((item) => hrefOf(item)), kind).toEqual(["/bookmarks"]);
      expect(items.filter((item) => item.includes('stroke-width="1.75"')).map((item) => hrefOf(item)), kind).toEqual(SIGNED_IN_ITEMS[kind].filter((href) => href !== "/bookmarks"));
      expect(textOf(nav), kind).toContain(UI_WORDS["nav.bookmarks"]);
    }
  });

  test("2d (decision 4, 10.1): Activity's item is its icon and its label alone, at every layout and on every page, Activity's own included", () => {
    for (const kind of KINDS) {
      for (const pathname of ["/", "/activity", "/settings/activity"]) {
        shell.kind = kind;
        shell.state = signedIn();
        shell.pathname = pathname;
        const nav = inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav\b[^>]*>/);
        const item = nav.split(/(?=<a\b)/).find((part) => hrefOf(part) === "/activity") ?? "";
        expect(item, `${kind} ${pathname}`).toContain("lucide-bell");
        // Nothing counts or badges: the item says its label and nothing else, no number, no dot, no other word.
        expect(textOf(inside(item, /<a\b[^>]*>/)), `${kind} ${pathname}`).toBe(UI_WORDS["nav.activity"]);
        expect(item, `${kind} ${pathname}`).not.toMatch(/aria-label=|aria-describedby=/);
        expect(nav.match(/<a\b/g), `${kind} ${pathname}`).toHaveLength(SIGNED_IN_ITEMS[kind].length);
      }
    }
  });

  test("on a phone the settings pages mark no nav item current: Settings is reached from the profile, and the settings row says where the reader is", () => {
    shell.kind = "phone";
    shell.state = signedIn();
    shell.pathname = "/settings/activity";
    const nav = inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav\b[^>]*>/);
    expect(anchors(nav).filter((tag) => tag.includes('aria-current="page"'))).toEqual([]);
    shell.pathname = "/activity";
    expect(anchors(inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav\b[^>]*>/)).filter((tag) => tag.includes('aria-current="page"')).map(hrefOf)).toEqual(["/activity"]);
  });

  test("signed out the nav holds Home and Sign in; while the session loads it holds Home alone, so Sign in never flashes", () => {
    for (const kind of KINDS) {
      shell.kind = kind;
      shell.state = { status: "signed-out" };
      expect(anchors(inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav [^>]*>/)).map(hrefOf), kind).toEqual(["/", "/signin", "/settings/appearance"]);
      shell.state = { status: "loading" };
      const loading = inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav\b[^>]*>/);
      expect(anchors(loading).map(hrefOf), kind).toEqual(["/"]);
      expect(textOf(loading), kind).not.toContain(UI_WORDS["nav.signin"]);
    }
  });

  test("Home is current on / only, Settings on every settings page, and the wordmark is the rail's k and the full nav's korbat", () => {
    shell.state = signedIn();
    shell.kind = "wide";
    shell.pathname = "/settings/cases";
    const current = (out: string) => anchors(inside(out, /<nav\b[^>]*>/)).filter((tag) => tag.includes('aria-current="page"')).map(hrefOf);
    expect(current(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>))).toEqual(["/settings"]);
    shell.pathname = "/";
    expect(current(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>))).toEqual(["/"]);
    shell.pathname = "/u/ada/followers";
    expect(current(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>))).toEqual(["/u/ada"]);
    expect(textOf(inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav\b[^>]*>/)).startsWith(UI_WORDS["frame.wordmark"])).toBe(true);
    shell.kind = "tablet";
    expect(textOf(inside(html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>), /<nav\b[^>]*>/)).startsWith("k ")).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the skip link comes first, says where it goes, and the main column it moves to takes the focus", () => {
    for (const kind of KINDS) {
      shell.kind = kind;
      const out = html(<AppShell>{null}</AppShell>);
      const first = anchors(out)[0] ?? "";
      expect(hrefOf(first), kind).toBe("#main");
      expect(textOf(inside(out, /<a\b[^>]*href="#main"[^>]*>/)), kind).toBe(UI_WORDS["shell.skip"]);
      const main = /<main\b[^>]*>/.exec(out)?.[0] ?? "";
      expect(main, kind).toContain('id="main"');
      expect(main, kind).toContain('tabindex="-1"');
      // The skip link, then the nav, then the main column, in that order in the page.
      expect(out.indexOf('href="#main"'), kind).toBeLessThan(out.indexOf("<nav"));
      expect(out.indexOf("<nav"), kind).toBeLessThan(out.indexOf("<main"));
    }
  });

  test("the shell keeps the standing banner and the floating compose button it is given", () => {
    const source = read("components", "AppShell.tsx");
    expect(source).toContain("<StandingBanner standing={state.me.standing} />");
    shell.kind = "phone";
    expect(html(<AppShell floating={<Text>floating control</Text>}>{null}</AppShell>)).toContain("floating control");
  });
});

describe("the context column (section 7.3, decision 14)", () => {

describe("the not-found screen and the error boundary (section 8.11)", () => {
  test("a mistyped address shows, inside the shell, that the page does not exist, with Go to Home, under its own title", () => {
    shell.kind = "wide";

    expect(anchors(inside(out, /<main\b[^>]*>/)).map(hrefOf)).toContain("/");
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain(UI_WORDS["notFound.action"]);
    expect(out).toContain(`<title>${TITLE_WORDS["title.notFound"]}</title>`);
  });

  test("the boundary draws the public frame with its words, Try again and Go to Home, and nothing of the error", () => {
    const retry = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const out = html(<ErrorBoundary error={new Error("secret detail of a broken screen")} retry={retry} />);
    expect(out).toContain("<header");
    expect(out).toContain("<main");
    expect(out).toMatch(new RegExp(`<h1[^>]*>${UI_WORDS["crash.title"]}</h1>`));
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain(UI_WORDS["crash.body"]);
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain(UI_WORDS["crash.retry"]);
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain(UI_WORDS["notFound.action"]);
    expect(out).not.toContain("secret detail");
    // Nothing about the error leaves the device: the layout sends nothing anywhere.
    expect(read("app", "_layout.tsx")).not.toMatch(/fetch\(|api\(|sendBeacon|console\./);
  });

  test("the root layout puts the gesture root and the safe areas outside, and the one Toaster inside the theme", () => {
    const layout = read("app", "_layout.tsx");
    expect(layout.indexOf("<GestureHandlerRootView")).toBeLessThan(layout.indexOf("<SafeAreaProvider"));
    expect(layout.indexOf("<SafeAreaProvider")).toBeLessThan(layout.indexOf("<ThemeProvider"));
    expect(layout.match(/<Toaster \/>/g)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(layout.indexOf("<ThemeProvider")).toBeLessThan(layout.indexOf("<Toaster />"));
    expect(layout.indexOf("<Toaster />")).toBeLessThan(layout.indexOf("</ThemeProvider>"));
    expect(layout).toContain("export function ErrorBoundary({ error, retry }: ErrorBoundaryProps)");
  });
});

describe("toasts (sections 5.4 and 6.16)", () => {
  test("show() hands sonner one custom toast for four seconds, eight with an action and six for a rollback", () => {
    expect(toastDuration({ message: "Link copied" })).toBe(4000);

  });

    expect(TOAST_LIMIT).toBe(3);

    expect(read("theme", "fonts.web.ts")).toContain(".k-still { transform: none !important; transition: opacity 150ms ease !important; }");
  });

  test("on native the same API announces the sentence, with the action's word, to the screen reader", () => {
    const native = read("components", "toast.tsx");
    expect(native).toContain('from "sonner-native"');
    expect(native).toContain("AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(");
  });
});

describe("the header that hides, and the soft reset (sections 5.2 and 7.1, review ruling 8)", () => {
  test("headerOffset(): down past the header's height hides it, any scroll up shows it, the top always shows it", () => {
    const at = (previousY: number, y: number, offset = 0) => headerOffset({ previousY, y, height: 60, offset });
    expect(at(0, 30)).toBe(0);
    expect(at(30, 90)).toBe(-60);
    expect(at(90, 120, -60)).toBe(-60);
    expect(at(120, 110, -60)).toBe(0);
    expect(at(110, 140, 0)).toBe(-60);
    expect(at(40, 50, 0)).toBe(0);
    expect(at(10, -5, -60)).toBe(0);
    expect(headerOffset({ previousY: 0, y: 500, height: 0, offset: 0 })).toBe(0);
  });

  test("the shell's scroll moves the header only when it changes, only on phones, and never under reduced motion", () => {
    const moves: number[] = [];
    const scrolled: boolean[] = [];
    const store = createShellScroll({ moveHeader: (offset) => moves.push(offset), markScrolled: (value) => scrolled.push(value) });
    store.settings = { hides: true, reduced: false };
    store.setHeight(60);
    for (const y of [20, 80, 120, 100, 160, 0]) store.onScroll(y);
    expect(moves).toEqual([-60, 0, -60, 0]);
    expect(scrolled).toEqual([true, false]);
    // Focus inside the header shows it.
    store.onScroll(200);
    store.show();
    expect(moves.slice(-2)).toEqual([-60, 0]);
    moves.length = 0;
    store.settings = { hides: false, reduced: true };
    for (const y of [20, 300, 600]) store.onScroll(y);
    expect(moves).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("pressing the current Home item again brings the registered list to its newest post, smooth, or at once under reduced motion", () => {
    const store = createShellScroll({ moveHeader: () => undefined, markScrolled: () => undefined });
    const toTop = vi.fn();
    const unregister = store.register({ toTop });
    const event = { preventDefault: vi.fn() };
    softReset(event, store);
    expect(event.preventDefault).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(toTop).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(true);
    store.settings = { hides: false, reduced: true };
    softReset(event, store);
    expect(toTop).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(false);
    unregister();
    expect(store.toTop()).toBe(false);
    // The shell gives this handler to the current Home item's link, and to no other item.
    const source = read("components", "AppShell.tsx");
    expect(source).toContain("onHomeAgain: (event) => softReset(event, scroll)");
    expect(source).toContain('const again = current && item.href === "/" ? onHomeAgain : undefined;');
  });

  test("the lists hand the shell their scroll and their way to the top, and the three screens title themselves through ScreenHeader", () => {
    const list = read("components", "list", "List.tsx");
    expect(list).toContain("scroll.onScroll(event);");
    expect(list).toContain("scroll.register(");
    for (const file of [["app", "bookmarks.tsx"], ["app", "u", "[handle]", "followers.tsx"], ["app", "u", "[handle]", "following.tsx"]]) {
      expect(read(...file), file.join("/")).toContain("<ScreenHeader");
    }
    const header = read("components", "ScreenHeader.tsx");
    expect(header).toContain('as="h1"');
    expect(header).toContain('variant="display-2"');
    expect(header).toContain('UI_WORDS["shell.back"]');
  });
});
```

```tsx
    expect(STANDING_TEXTS.banner.running(ENDS)).toBe(

    );
    expect(STANDING_TEXTS.banner.label).toBe("Your account's standing");
    expect(STANDING_TEXTS.refused.suspended(ENDS)).toBe(`Your account is suspended until ${standingTime(ENDS)}, so you cannot do this now.`);
    expect(STANDING_TEXTS.refused.terminated).toBe("korbat has terminated your account, so you cannot do this.");
    expect(STANDING_TEXTS.refused.over).toBe("The suspension has just ended. Try again.");
    expect(STANDING_TEXTS.report.suspended(ENDS)).toBe(

    expect(refusalSentence(NONE)).toBe(STANDING_TEXTS.refused.over);
    expect(refusalSentence(null)).toBe(STANDING_TEXTS.refused.over);

    expect(runningMeasure(running({ state: "announced" }))).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("3e: the report form, Your standing and Settings, Profile while the suspension runs (design, sections 9.4 to 9.6)", () => {
  test("the report form disables its first choice with [report.suspended], and leaves the notice of illegality and the path for child sexual abuse material open", () => {
    const out = html(<ReportForm signedIn given={{ kind: "post", id: id(1) }} standing={running()} />);
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain(STANDING_TEXTS.report.suspended(ENDS));

    expect(plain).toContain(STANDING_TEXTS.refused.suspended(ENDS));
    expect(plain).not.toContain(STANDING_TEXTS.handle.retiredSuspended);
    expect(read("app", "settings", "profile.tsx")).toContain("{refusalSentence(me.standing)}");
  });
```

```ts
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import path from "node:path";
import { createElement } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";
import * as lucide from "lucide-react";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { FONT_FACES, FONT_FAMILY, fontFaceCss } from "@/theme/fonts.web";
import { SYSTEM_MONO_STACK, SYSTEM_STACK, TEXT_STEPS, Text, VARIANTS, stepped, textStyle, type TextVariant } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { Icon } from "@/components/kit/Icon";
import { ICONS, type IconName } from "@/components/icons";
import { BREAKPOINTS, GUTTER, layoutKind } from "@/theme/layout";
import { MOTION } from "@/theme/motion";
import { LEGACY_COLOUR_FILES, SRC, sourceFiles } from "./legacy-files";

/**
 * The type, the fonts and the other constants of the design language (UI design, sections 4.3 to 4.7, 5.1 and 7.1):
 * the bundled font files exist and are declared as their packages declare them, their licences sit beside the app,
 * the text-size step's maths, the variants, and the icons' closed list.
 */
const APP = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..");
const requireFromApp = createRequire(path.join(APP, "package.json"));
const PACKAGES = ["@fontsource-variable/fraunces", "@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next", "@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-mono"];

/** The package CSS's @font-face rule for one woff2 file, as its fields. */
function packageRule(file: string): Record<string, string> {
  const pkg = file.split("/files/")[0]!;
  const name = file.split("/files/")[1]!;
  const dir = path.dirname(requireFromApp.resolve(`${pkg}/package.json`));
  for (const css of ["full.css", "full-italic.css", "wght.css", "wght-italic.css"]) {
    if (!existsSync(path.join(dir, css))) continue;
    for (const block of readFileSync(path.join(dir, css), "utf8").matchAll(/@font-face\s*\{([^}]*)\}/g)) {
      if (!block[1]!.includes(`./files/${name})`)) continue;
      return Object.fromEntries([...block[1]!.matchAll(/([a-z-]+)\s*:\s*([^;]+);/g)].map((match) => [match[1]!, match[2]!.trim()]));
    }
  }
  throw new Error(`no rule in ${pkg} names ${name}`);
}

describe("the fonts", () => {
  const source = readFileSync(path.join(SRC, "theme", "fonts.web.ts"), "utf8");
  const required = [...source.matchAll(/require\("([^"]+)"\)/g)].map((match) => match[1]!);

  test("fonts.web.ts requires each face's file by its literal path, and every one of them exists", () => {
    expect(required.sort()).toEqual(FONT_FACES.map((face) => face.file).sort());
    for (const file of required) expect(existsSync(requireFromApp.resolve(file)), file).toBe(true);
    for (const face of FONT_FACES) expect(face.url.toString(), face.file).toContain(face.file);
  });

  test("the three families come as their packages ship them: Fraunces' full axes, the text face's roman and italic, the mono roman; latin and latin-ext each", () => {
    expect(FONT_FACES.map((face) => face.file.split("/files/")[1]).sort()).toEqual([
      "atkinson-hyperlegible-mono-latin-ext-wght-normal.woff2",
      "atkinson-hyperlegible-mono-latin-wght-normal.woff2",
      "atkinson-hyperlegible-next-latin-ext-wght-italic.woff2",
      "atkinson-hyperlegible-next-latin-ext-wght-normal.woff2",
      "atkinson-hyperlegible-next-latin-wght-italic.woff2",
      "atkinson-hyperlegible-next-latin-wght-normal.woff2",
      "fraunces-latin-ext-full-normal.woff2",
      "fraunces-latin-full-normal.woff2",
    ]);
    expect(FONT_FAMILY).toEqual({ display: "Fraunces Variable", text: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable", mono: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono Variable" });
  });

  test("each rule's family, style, weights and unicode-range equal the package CSS's, so latin-ext downloads only when a post needs it", () => {
    for (const face of FONT_FACES) {
      const rule = packageRule(face.file);
      expect(`'${face.family}'`, face.file).toBe(rule["font-family"]);
      expect(face.style, face.file).toBe(rule["font-style"]);
      expect(face.weight, face.file).toBe(rule["font-weight"]);
      expect(face.unicodeRange, face.file).toBe(rule["unicode-range"]);
    }
  });

  test("the style element's rules swap in once loaded and name the bundled file's URL", () => {
    const css = fontFaceCss((face) => `/assets/${face.file.split("/files/")[1]}`);
    expect(css.match(/@font-face/g)).toHaveLength(FONT_FACES.length);
    expect(css.match(/font-display: swap;/g)).toHaveLength(FONT_FACES.length);
    expect(css).toContain('src: url("/assets/fraunces-latin-full-normal.woff2") format("woff2-variations");');
    expect(css).not.toMatch(/https?:/);
  });

  test("each package's licence, the SIL Open Font License, sits in assets/fonts/LICENSES as the package ships it", () => {
    for (const pkg of PACKAGES) {
      const shipped = readFileSync(requireFromApp.resolve(`${pkg}/LICENSE`), "utf8");
      const kept = path.join(APP, "assets", "fonts", "LICENSES", `${pkg.split("/")[1]}-OFL.txt`);
      expect(existsSync(kept), kept).toBe(true);
      expect(readFileSync(kept, "utf8"), pkg).toBe(shipped);
      expect(shipped).toContain("SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1");
    }
  });
});

describe("the type scale", () => {
  test("the ten variants have section 4.3's faces, weights, sizes, line heights and tracking, and 6.6's large post text", () => {
    const table: Record<TextVariant, [string, number, number, number, number]> = {
      "display-1": ["display", 600, 34, 40, -0.02],
      "display-2": ["display", 600, 28, 34, -0.015],
      "display-3": ["display", 600, 22, 28, -0.01],
      title: ["text", 700, 18, 24, 0],
      post: ["text", 400, 17, 26, 0],
      // The thread's focused post (6.6): the post's face at 19 / 28.
      "post-large": ["text", 400, 19, 28, 0],
      body: ["text", 400, 15, 22, 0],
      "body-strong": ["text", 700, 15, 22, 0],
      meta: ["text", 400, 13, 18, 0.005],
      chip: ["text", 700, 12, 16, 0.01],
      mono: ["mono", 400, 14, 20, 0],
    };
    expect(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(VARIANTS).map(([name, v]) => [name, [v.face, v.weight, v.size, v.line, v.tracking]]))).toEqual(table);
  });

  test("Fraunces is used at 22 px and up only, at the Default step", () => {
    for (const [name, variant] of Object.entries(VARIANTS)) if (variant.face === "display") expect(variant.size, name).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(22);
  });

  test("the text-size step multiplies size and line height together, rounded to whole pixels", () => {
    expect(TEXT_STEPS).toEqual({ smaller: 0.875, default: 1, larger: 1.125, largest: 1.25 });
    expect([stepped(17, "smaller"), stepped(26, "smaller"), stepped(17, "default"), stepped(15, "larger"), stepped(22, "larger"), stepped(34, "largest"), stepped(13, "largest")]).toEqual([15, 23, 17, 17, 25, 43, 16]);
  });

  test("on web sizes are rem, so the browser's own text size scales them too, with tracking in em", () => {
    const post = textStyle("post", { step: "smaller", font: "korbat" }, "web");
    expect(post).toMatchObject({ fontSize: "0.9375rem", lineHeight: "1.4375rem", fontWeight: "400" });
    expect(post.fontFamily).toBe(`"Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable", ${SYSTEM_STACK}`);
    const display = textStyle("display-1", { step: "default", font: "korbat" }, "web");
    expect(display).toMatchObject({ fontSize: "2.125rem", lineHeight: "2.5rem", letterSpacing: "-0.02em", fontWeight: "600" });
    expect(display.fontFamily).toBe(`"Fraunces Variable", ${SYSTEM_STACK}`);
    expect(textStyle("mono", { step: "default", font: "korbat" }, "web").fontFamily).toBe(`"Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono Variable", ${SYSTEM_MONO_STACK}`);
  });

  test("with the system font, text and display take the system stack (display at 700) and mono the system monospace", () => {
    expect(SYSTEM_STACK).toBe('system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif');
    expect(SYSTEM_MONO_STACK).toBe('ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, monospace');
    const display = textStyle("display-1", { step: "default", font: "system" }, "web");
    expect(display).toMatchObject({ fontFamily: SYSTEM_STACK, fontWeight: "700" });
    expect(display).not.toHaveProperty("fontVariationSettings");
    expect(textStyle("mono", { step: "default", font: "system" }, "web").fontFamily).toBe(SYSTEM_MONO_STACK);
  });

  test("on native sizes are pixels times the step, the system font is every family, and the OS text size is capped on chrome only", () => {
    const families = { display: undefined, text: undefined, mono: undefined };
    const post = textStyle("post", { step: "larger", font: "korbat" }, "native", families);
    expect(post).toMatchObject({ fontSize: 19, lineHeight: 29, fontWeight: "400" });

});

describe("the layout and motion constants", () => {
  test("useLayout's four kinds start at 768, 1024 and 1280 px; the gutter is 16 px on phones and 20 px wider", () => {
    expect(BREAKPOINTS).toEqual({ tablet: 768, desktop: 1024, wide: 1280 });
    expect([320, 767, 768, 1023, 1024, 1279, 1280, 1920].map(layoutKind)).toEqual(["phone", "phone", "tablet", "tablet", "desktop", "desktop", "wide", "wide"]);
    expect(GUTTER).toEqual({ phone: 16, wider: 20 });
  });

  test("motion.ts holds section 5.1's six values as plain data", () => {
    expect(MOTION).toEqual({
      easeOut: { type: "timing", easing: [0.23, 1, 0.32, 1] },
      easeInOut: { type: "timing", easing: [0.77, 0, 0.175, 1] },
      springSnap: { type: "spring", dampingRatio: 1, duration: 300 },
      springRelease: { type: "spring", dampingRatio: 0.85, duration: 350 },
      press: { type: "timing", in: 100, out: 160, easing: [0.23, 1, 0.32, 1] },
      fade: { type: "timing", duration: 150, easing: [0.23, 1, 0.32, 1] },
    });
  });

  test("tailwind.config.js adds section 4.5's five radii", () => {
    const config = requireFromApp("./tailwind.config.js") as { theme: { extend: { borderRadius: Record<string, string> } } };
    expect(config.theme.extend.borderRadius).toEqual({ control: "10px", media: "12px", card: "16px", sheet: "24px", full: "9999px" });
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { AppState, Platform, Pressable, View } from "react-native";
import { Link, Redirect, router, useIsFocused, useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import type { ActivityEntry, ActivityTab } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { FollowsEntry } from "@/components/activity/FollowsEntry";
import { ModerationEntry } from "@/components/activity/ModerationEntry";
import { PostEntry } from "@/components/activity/PostEntry";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { EmptyState } from "@/components/kit/EmptyState";
import { ErrorState } from "@/components/kit/ErrorState";
import { Icon } from "@/components/kit/Icon";
import { FOCUS_RING } from "@/components/kit/interaction";
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/kit/Skeleton";
import { TabPanel, Tabs } from "@/components/kit/Tabs";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { List, useStable, type ListHandle } from "@/components/list/List";
import { HeaderSpace, ScreenHeader } from "@/components/ScreenHeader";
import { renderFeedRow } from "@/components/social/FeedRows";
import { NewPostsPill } from "@/components/social/NewPostsPill";
import {
  activityApi,
  activityEnd,
  activityPill,
  activityPollActive,
  activityRows,
  activityTab,
  createActivityPoll,
  firstEntryKey,
  firstLoadedKey,
  markForVisit,
  retryFocus,
  seenToSend,
  type ActivityRow,
} from "@/lib/activity";
import { ACTIVITY_WORDS } from "@/lib/activity-words";
import { errorMessage } from "@/lib/api";
import { pageVisible } from "@/lib/new-posts";
import { usePageTitle } from "@/lib/page-title";
import { useSession } from "@/lib/session";
import { useShellScroll } from "@/lib/shell-scroll";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";

const W = ACTIVITY_WORDS;
/** The panel the tabs control. */
const PANEL = "activity-panel";

/**
 * "New since you last looked" and "Earlier" (10.2): h2s, so headings navigation reaches both, drawn as the feed's "You
 * were here" is, a label and a line in ink-medium, never a colour alone.
 */
function Heading({ heading }: { heading: "new" | "earlier" }) {
  return (
    <View className="flex-row items-center gap-3 px-4 pb-2 pt-4">
      <Text as="h2" variant="body-strong" tone="medium">
        {heading === "new" ? W["activity.divider"] : W["activity.earlier"]}
      </Text>
      <View className="h-px flex-1 bg-line-high" />
    </View>
  );
}

/** What a list row needs besides itself; the feed's rows are reused for the skeletons and Load more. */
export interface ActivityRowProps {
  row: ActivityRow;
  tab: ActivityTab;
  /** The reader's handle: a follow group's "See your followers" opens their own list. */
  handle: string;
  onRetry: () => void;
  onLoadMore: () => void;
}

const noop = () => undefined;

/** One row of the list: an entry by its type, a heading, or the list's own states (10.2). */
export function ActivityRowView({ row, tab, handle, onRetry, onLoadMore }: ActivityRowProps) {
  switch (row.kind) {
    case "entry":
      return row.entry.type === "post" ? <PostEntry entry={row.entry} /> : row.entry.type === "follows" ? <FollowsEntry entry={row.entry} handle={handle} /> : <ModerationEntry entry={row.entry} />;
    case "heading":
      return <Heading heading={row.heading} />;
    case "empty":
      return tab === "all" ? <EmptyState title={W["activity.empty.all.title"]} body={W["activity.empty.all.body"]} /> : <EmptyState title={W["activity.empty.conversations.title"]} body={W["activity.empty.conversations.body"]} />;
    case "error":
      return <ErrorState message={W["activity.error"]} onRetry={onRetry} />;
    case "end":
      return (
        <View className="items-center px-4 py-8">
          <Text variant="meta" tone="low" className="text-center">
            {activityEnd()}
          </Text>
        </View>
      );
    default:
      return renderFeedRow(row, { renderPost: () => null, setSize: -1, index: 0, empty: { body: "" }, onRetry, onLoadMore });
  }
}

/** The header's quiet link to Settings, Activity (10.1): the settings icon and its words in ink-medium, 44 px tall. */
function SettingsLink() {
  return (
    <Link href="/settings/activity" asChild>
      <Pressable className={cn("min-h-[44px] flex-row items-center gap-1.5 self-start rounded-control active:opacity-70", FOCUS_RING)}>
        <Icon name="settings" size={16} tone="medium" />
        <Text variant="meta" tone="medium" className="underline web:underline-offset-2">
          {W["activity.settingsLink"]}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  );
}

function Header({ tab }: { tab: ActivityTab }) {
  return (
    <ScreenHeader title={W["activity.title"]}>
      <SettingsLink />
      <Tabs
        label={W["activity.tabs"]}
        tabs={[
          { key: "all", label: W["activity.tab.all"] },
          { key: "conversations", label: W["activity.tab.conversations"] },
        ]}
        selected={tab}
        // The tab lives in the address, so a reload keeps it; nothing is stored.
        onSelect={(next) => router.setParams({ tab: next })}
        panelId={PANEL}
      />
    </ScreenHeader>
  );
}

interface ListState {
  items: ActivityEntry[];
  cursor: string | null;
  status: "loading" | "ready" | "error";
  error: string | null;
  loadingMore: boolean;
  moreError: string | null;
}

const LOADING: ListState = { items: [], cursor: null, status: "loading", error: null, loadingMore: false, moreError: null };

/**
 * On the web, moves the focus to the entry whose row has this key, its article, which takes the focus by script; true once
 * it holds the focus, false while the row is not drawn yet. Native has no such element, so there is nothing to wait for.
 */
function focusEntry(key: string): boolean {
  if (Platform.OS !== "web" || typeof document === "undefined") return true;
  const article = document.querySelector(`[data-row="${key}"] [role="article"]`) as HTMLElement | null;
  article?.focus();
  return article !== null && document.activeElement === article;
}

/**
 * One tab's list (2d design, sections 5.7, 5.8 and 10.2): the first page, then the seen marker with its newest time when
 * something on it was new; later pages marked new against the first page's marker; the newer count asked 30 s after the
 * list opened and every 60 s, only while the screen is focused and the page visible, shown in the feed's pill; the pill,
 * and pull to refresh on phones, read the first page again at the top, and the focus goes to the first entry; after Load
 * more, to the first entry it brought. Nothing here outlives the screen, and nothing else in the app asks for Activity.
 */
function ActivityList({ tab, handle }: { tab: ActivityTab; handle: string }) {
  const focused = useIsFocused();
  const scroll = useShellScroll();
  const [state, setState] = useState<ListState>(LOADING);
  const [newer, setNewer] = useState(0);
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(pageVisible);
  const [refreshing, setRefreshing] = useState(false);
  // The first page's marker, kept for the visit: later pages are new against it, not against the marker this visit sent.
  const visit = useRef<string | null>(null);
  const focusNext = useRef<string | null>(null);
  // The focus request still waiting for its row to be drawn; a newer request, or the list's end, cancels it.
  const pendingFocus = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null);
  const cancelFocus = () => {
    pendingFocus.current?.();
    pendingFocus.current = null;
  };
  const list = useRef<ListHandle>(null);
  const latest = useRef(state);
  latest.current = state;

  const first = useStable(async (focus: boolean) => {
    try {
      const page = await activityApi.page(tab);
      visit.current = page.seenAt;
      setNewer(0);
      setState({ ...LOADING, items: page.items, cursor: page.nextCursor, status: "ready" });
      if (focus) {
        // The pill and a refresh show the first page at the top, where the focus goes.
        list.current?.toTop(false);
        focusNext.current = page.items[0]?.key ?? null;
      }
      const seen = seenToSend(page);
      if (seen !== null) void activityApi.seen(seen).catch(noop);
    } catch (err) {
      setState({ ...LOADING, status: "error", error: errorMessage(err) });
    }
  });
  useEffect(() => {
    void first(false);
  }, [tab]);

  const more = useStable(async () => {
    const now = latest.current;
    if (now.cursor === null || now.loadingMore) return;
    cancelFocus();
    setState({ ...now, loadingMore: true, moreError: null });
    try {
      const page = await activityApi.page(tab, now.cursor);
      focusNext.current = firstLoadedKey(now.items.length, [...now.items, ...page.items]);
      setState({ ...now, items: [...now.items, ...markForVisit(page.items, visit.current)], cursor: page.nextCursor, loadingMore: false, moreError: null });
    } catch (err) {
      setState({ ...now, loadingMore: false, moreError: errorMessage(err) });
    }
  });
  const reload = useStable(async () => {
    cancelFocus();
    setRefreshing(true);
    await first(true);
    setRefreshing(false);
  });

  // The focus moves to the entry the pill, a refresh or Load more names once its row is drawn. The list draws only a window
  // of rows, in batches, and on a slow device the window can still be elsewhere when the page lands (the removed Load more
  // row takes the scroll with it): so it is tried until the row's article is there and holds the focus, for a few seconds
  // at most, and while the row is not drawn the list is asked to draw the rows around it.
  useEffect(() => {
    const key = focusNext.current;
    focusNext.current = null;
    if (key === null) return;
    cancelFocus();
    pendingFocus.current = retryFocus(() => {
      if (focusEntry(key)) return true;
      list.current?.jumpTo(key, false);
      return false;
    });
  }, [state]);
  useEffect(() => cancelFocus, []);

  // The page's visibility, as the feed follows it: the poll stops while korbat is in the background.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (Platform.OS === "web" && typeof document !== "undefined") {
      const change = () => setVisible(pageVisible());
      document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", change);
      return () => document.removeEventListener("visibilitychange", change);
    }
    const subscription = AppState.addEventListener("change", (next) => setVisible(next === "active"));
    return () => subscription.remove();
  }, []);

  const ask = useStable(async () => {
    const answer = await activityApi.newer(tab, latest.current.items[0]?.at);
    setNewer(answer.count);
  });
  const clock = useRef<ReturnType<typeof createActivityPoll> | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const made = createActivityPoll(ask);
    clock.current = made;
    return () => made.dispose();
  }, [tab]);
  useEffect(() => {
    clock.current?.setActive(activityPollActive({ focused, visible, ready: state.status === "ready" }));
  }, [focused, visible, state.status]);

  const rows = activityRows(state);
  const retry = useStable(() => {
    setState(LOADING);
    void first(false);
  });
  return (
    <View className="flex-1">
      <List
        handle={list}
        rows={rows}
        keyOf={(row) => row.key}
        versionOf={(row) => (row.kind === "entry" ? [row.entry] : row.kind === "loadMore" ? [row.busy] : row.kind === "loadMoreError" || row.kind === "error" ? [row.message] : [row.kind])}
        renderRow={(row) => <ActivityRowView row={row} tab={tab} handle={handle} onRetry={retry} onLoadMore={() => void more()} />}
        feed
        label={W["activity.title"]}
        busy={state.status === "loading" || state.loadingMore}
        refreshing={refreshing}
        onRefresh={Platform.OS === "web" ? undefined : () => void reload()}
      />
      <NewPostsPill count={newer} top={scroll.headerSpace} headerY={scroll.headerY} onPress={() => void reload()} wordsFor={activityPill} label={W["activity.pill.label"]} />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * Activity (2d design, section 10.2; decisions 4 to 6): for an account only, signed out it goes to Sign in, as Bookmarks
 * does. The header "Activity" with the quiet link to its settings and the tabs All and Conversations, the tab in the
 * address (`?tab=conversations`); then the tab's list. The screen is the only place that asks for or shows what is new.
 */
export default function Activity() {
  const { state } = useSession();
  const title = usePageTitle("title.activity");
  const { tab: param } = useLocalSearchParams<{ tab?: string }>();
  const tab = activityTab(param);
  if (state.status === "signed-out") return <Redirect href="/signin" />;
  if (state.status === "signed-in" && !state.me.user.onboarded) return <Redirect href="/handle" />;
  return (
    <AppShell>
      {title}
      <Header tab={tab} />
      <TabPanel panelId={PANEL} selected={tab}>
        {state.status === "signed-in" ? (
          <ActivityList key={tab} tab={tab} handle={state.me.profile?.handle ?? ""} />
        ) : (
          <>
            <HeaderSpace />
            <Skeleton.List kind="posts" count={5} />
          </>
        )}
      </TabPanel>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

### Create `apps/app/src/app/settings/activity.tsx`

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Platform, View } from "react-native";
import type { ActivityReach, ActivitySettings } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { ListRow, RadioGroup } from "@/components/kit/ListRow";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { ScreenHeader, ScreenScroll } from "@/components/ScreenHeader";
import { SettingsNav } from "@/components/SettingsNav";
import { toast } from "@/components/toast";
import { Body, ErrorText, Section, SectionRows } from "@/components/ui";
import { activityApi, createSettingsSaver } from "@/lib/activity";
import { errorMessage } from "@/lib/api";
import { usePageTitle } from "@/lib/page-title";
import { ACTIVITY_SETTINGS_WORDS as S } from "@/lib/settings-words";

/** The three reaches in their order, by their words (decision 7). */
const REACHES: [ActivityReach, string][] = [
  ["everyone", S.everyone],
  ["older", S.older],
  ["following", S.following],
  ["off", S.off],
];

const GROUPS = [
  ["replies", S.replies],
  ["mentions", S.mentions],
  ["quotes", S.quotes],
] as const;

/**
 * A radio group's card, which says when the focus has left it (10.8): on the web, focus moving outside the group (or
 * out of the page) saves its choice at once instead of after the 800 ms.
 */
function Group({ id, title, onLeave, children }: { id: string; title: string; onLeave: () => void; children: ReactNode }) {
  const leave = {
    onBlur: (event: { currentTarget: Element; relatedTarget: Element | null }) => {
      if (!event.relatedTarget || !event.currentTarget.contains(event.relatedTarget)) onLeave();
    },
  };
  return (
    <Section title={title} id={id}>
      <SectionRows end>
        <View {...(Platform.OS === "web" ? (leave as object) : {})}>
          <RadioGroup labelledBy={id}>{children}</RadioGroup>
        </View>
      </SectionRows>
    </Section>
  );
}

/**
 * The four groups (10.8): Replies to your posts, Mentions of you and Quotes of your posts (Everyone, Accounts older than 2
 * days, Accounts you follow, Off) and New followers (On, Off), each one tab stop whose arrows move the choice, as
 * Appearance's are. `onChoose` takes the whole settings with one value changed; `onLeave` is the focus leaving a group.
 */
export function ActivitySettingsForm({ value, onChoose, onLeave }: { value: ActivitySettings; onChoose: (next: ActivitySettings) => void; onLeave: () => void }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Body>{S.intro}</Body>
      {GROUPS.map(([field, title]) => (
        <Group key={field} id={`activity-${field}`} title={title} onLeave={onLeave}>
          {REACHES.map(([reach, label]) => (
            <ListRow key={reach} label={label} control={{ kind: "radio", checked: value[field] === reach, onSelect: () => onChoose({ ...value, [field]: reach }) }} />
          ))}
        </Group>
      ))}
      <Group id="activity-follows" title={S.follows} onLeave={onLeave}>
        {([true, false] as const).map((on) => (
          <ListRow key={String(on)} label={on ? S.on : S.off} control={{ kind: "radio", checked: value.follows === on, onSelect: () => onChoose({ ...value, follows: on }) }} />
        ))}
      </Group>
      <Text tone="medium" className="mt-6">
        {S.muted}
      </Text>
      <Text tone="medium" className="mt-2">
        {S.fromNow}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * Settings, Activity (2d design, decisions 7 and 8, section 10.8): who may reach the person in Activity. Unlike
 * Appearance's, the choices are the server's: the screen reads them, shows a choice at once, and saves it once it has
 * settled (lib/activity.ts's createSettingsSaver): one request and one toast, "Saved", per settled change; a refused save
 * puts the saved choice back and says so.
 */
export default function ActivitySettingsScreen() {
  const title = usePageTitle("title.settingsActivity");
  const [value, setValue] = useState<ActivitySettings | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const saver = useRef<ReturnType<typeof createSettingsSaver> | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    let current = true;
    activityApi.settings().then(
      (settings) => {
        if (!current) return;
        setValue(settings);
        saver.current = createSettingsSaver({
          initial: settings,
          save: activityApi.saveSettings,
          onSaved: () => toast.show({ message: S.saved }),
          onFailed: (saved) => {
            setValue(saved);
            toast.show({ message: S.failed, tone: "rollback" });
          },
        });
      },
      (err: unknown) => {
        if (current) setError(errorMessage(err));
      },
    );
    return () => {
      current = false;
      // A choice still waiting is saved as the screen goes, as leaving its group would save it.
      saver.current?.leave();
      saver.current?.dispose();
    };
  }, []);
  return (
    <AppShell>
      {title}
      <ScreenHeader title={S.nav}>
        <SettingsNav current="activity" />
      </ScreenHeader>
      <ScreenScroll screen="settings-activity">
        <ErrorText message={error} />
        {value ? (
          <ActivitySettingsForm
            value={value}
            onChoose={(next) => {
              setValue(next);
              saver.current?.choose(next);
            }}
            onLeave={() => saver.current?.leave()}
          />
        ) : null}
      </ScreenScroll>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Pressable, View } from "react-native";
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import type { ActivityEntry } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Avatar } from "@/components/kit/Avatar";
import { FOCUS_RING } from "@/components/kit/interaction";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { ACTIVITY_WORDS } from "@/lib/activity-words";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";
import { EntryArticle, EntryLine } from "./PostEntry";

type FollowsItem = Extract<ActivityEntry, { type: "follows" }>;

/**
 * The follows of one UTC day (2d design, decision 6, sections 5.5.3 and 10.2): up to three 32 px avatars side by side,
 * the line ("Ada and 4 others followed you") and the time of the newest follow, never the day itself. The row is not
 * pressable: each account shown is its own link to its profile, its avatar in a 44 px target named by its display name
 * (the line names one or two of them, so the avatars are where all three are), and a group of more than three ends with
 * "See your followers", the account's own Followers list.
 */
export function FollowsEntry({ entry, handle }: { entry: FollowsItem; handle: string }) {
  return (
    <EntryArticle entry={entry} className="gap-1 border-b border-line-low px-4 py-3">
      <View className="-ml-1.5 flex-row">
        {entry.actors.map((actor) => (
          <Link key={actor.id} href={`/u/${actor.handle}`} asChild>
            <Pressable aria-label={actor.displayName} className={cn("h-11 w-11 items-center justify-center rounded-full", FOCUS_RING)}>
              <Avatar account={actor} size={32} src={actor.avatar} />
            </Pressable>
          </Link>
        ))}
      </View>
      <EntryLine entry={entry} />
      {entry.count > 3 ? (
        <Link href={`/u/${handle}/followers`} asChild>
          <Pressable className={cn("min-h-[44px] justify-center self-start rounded-control", FOCUS_RING)}>
            <Text tone="accent" className="underline web:underline-offset-2">
              {ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.follow.all"]}
            </Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      ) : null}
    </EntryArticle>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Pressable, View } from "react-native";
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { AboutCard } from "@/components/AboutCard";
import { HandleBox } from "@/components/HandleBox";
import { FOCUS_RING } from "@/components/kit/interaction";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { UI_WORDS } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";
import { useLayout } from "@/theme/layout";

/** One row's target: its words in accent ink, underlined, 44 px tall, as every link of a card is. */
const TARGET = cn("min-h-[44px] justify-center self-start rounded-control active:opacity-70", FOCUS_RING);

function Words({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <Text tone="accent" className="underline web:underline-offset-2">
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}

function Row({ href, label }: { href: string; label: string }) {
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable className={TARGET}>
        <Words>{label}</Words>
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  );
}

/**
 * Getting started (2d design, decision 25, section 10.7): what an account's empty Following shows instead of the empty
 * state, until the first followed account posts. Its heading and one sentence, then one line and one link each: Latest
 * (which switches Home's tab), Explore and how it picks, the handle box itself (which phones see nowhere else), the
 * profile's settings (with where Settings is on a phone, 10.1) and the rules; below 1024 px, where the context column is
 * not drawn, How korbat works. Nothing is suggested by name, nothing is stored, and nothing is dismissed.
 */
export function GettingStarted({ onShowLatest }: { onShowLatest: () => void }) {
  const layout = useLayout();
  return (
    <View className="gap-4 px-4 py-6">
      <View className="gap-1 rounded-card border border-line-low bg-surface-1 px-4 pb-3 pt-4">
        <Text as="h2" variant="title">
          {UI_WORDS["feed.start.title"]}
        </Text>
        <Text tone="medium">{UI_WORDS["feed.start.body"]}</Text>
        <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={onShowLatest} className={cn(TARGET, "mt-2")}>
          <Words>{UI_WORDS["feed.start.latest"]}</Words>
        </Pressable>
        <Row href="/explore/about" label={UI_WORDS["feed.start.explore"]} />
        <View className="gap-2 py-2">
          <Text tone="medium">{UI_WORDS["feed.start.handle"]}</Text>
          <HandleBox />
        </View>
        <Row href="/settings/profile" label={UI_WORDS["feed.start.profile"]} />
        {layout === "phone" ? (
          <Text variant="meta" tone="low">
            {UI_WORDS["feed.start.settings"]}
          </Text>
        ) : null}
        <Row href="/rules" label={UI_WORDS["feed.start.rules"]} />
      </View>
      {layout === "phone" || layout === "tablet" ? <AboutCard /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import type { ActivityEntry } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ListRow } from "@/components/kit/ListRow";
import { activityWhen, entryLine } from "@/lib/activity";
import { ACTIVITY_WORDS } from "@/lib/activity-words";
import { EntryArticle } from "./PostEntry";

type ModerationItem = Extract<ActivityEntry, { type: "moderation" }>;

/** Where a notice opens (5.5.3): its screen under Settings, Cases, or the post for a lost image. */
export function moderationHref(entry: ModerationItem): string {
  if (entry.kind === "release") return `/settings/cases/releases/${entry.id}`;
  if (entry.kind === "upload") return `/settings/cases/uploads/${entry.id}`;
  if (entry.kind === "lost") return `/post/${entry.postId}`;
  return `/settings/cases/${entry.id}`;
}

/**
 * A notice korbat told the person about their own content or account (2d design, sections 5.5.2, 5.5.3 and 10.2): a link
 * row with the scales the Cases screen uses, the line, the time the person was told, and "Open in Cases" where it opens
 * under Cases; a lost image opens its post, so its row says nothing of Cases.
 */
export function ModerationEntry({ entry }: { entry: ModerationItem }) {
  return (
    <EntryArticle entry={entry}>
      <ListRow label={entryLine(entry)} description={activityWhen(entry.at)} icon="cases" href={moderationHref(entry)} value={entry.kind === "lost" ? undefined : ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.moderation.open"]} />
    </EntryArticle>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { View } from "react-native";
import type { ActivityEntry } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { PostCard } from "@/components/social/PostCard";
import { activityWhen, entryLine, entryName } from "@/lib/activity";
import { ACTIVITY_WORDS } from "@/lib/activity-words";
import { fill } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";
import { FOCUS_RING_INSET } from "@/components/kit/interaction";

type PostItem = Extract<ActivityEntry, { type: "post" }>;

/**
 * Every row of Activity is an article named by its line and its time, "New, " first while it is new (10.2), so a screen
 * reader moving by item hears what each is and which are new. It takes the focus by script only (after the pill, a
 * refresh or Load more), with the ring drawn inside, as a row's.
 */
export function EntryArticle({ entry, children, className }: { entry: ActivityEntry; children: ReactNode; className?: string }) {
  return (
    <View role="article" aria-label={entryName(entry)} tabIndex={-1} className={cn(FOCUS_RING_INSET, className)}>
      {children}
    </View>
  );
}

/** The line and the time as the row shows them, in meta, ink-medium; the article's name says the same, so it is hidden. */
export function EntryLine({ entry, children }: { entry: ActivityEntry; children?: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Text aria-hidden variant="meta" tone="medium">
      {children ?? fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.entry.name"], { line: entryLine(entry), time: activityWhen(entry.at) })}
    </Text>
  );
}

/**
 * A reply, a mention or a quote (2d design, sections 5.5.3 and 10.2): the line, then the post as PostCard's quiet card,
 * with the actor's 40 px avatar, its links, its images, its body opening the post, and one action, Reply, which opens the
 * thread with the reply card open, as the feed's Reply does, since each entry is a conversation to answer. No Like or
 * Repost keeps the row quiet; nothing is highlighted by colour.
 */
export function PostEntry({ entry }: { entry: PostItem }) {
  return (
    <EntryArticle entry={entry} className="border-b border-line-low pt-3">
      <View className="pl-[68px] pr-4">
        <EntryLine entry={entry} />
      </View>
      <PostCard post={entry.post} quiet />
    </EntryArticle>
  );
}
```

```ts
/**

 * `{time}` lib/time.ts's spoken time and `{date}` its day; fill() in lib/ui-words.ts puts them in. A release's, a refused
 * upload's and a lost image's lines are 3d's words unchanged (RELEASE_TEXTS.entry, UPLOAD_TEXTS.entry and
 * IMAGE_LOST_NOTICE.mail), which lib/activity.ts reads from their own modules.

export const ACTIVITY_WORDS = {
  "activity.title": "Activity",

  "activity.divider": "New since you last looked",
  "activity.earlier": "Earlier",
  "activity.pill.one": "1 new",
  "activity.pill": "{n} new",
  "activity.pill.many": "20+ new",
  "activity.pill.label": "{visible} above, go to the first one",
  "activity.reply": "{name} replied to your post",

  "activity.empty.conversations.title": "No conversations yet",

  "activity.end": "That's everything from the last {days} days.",
```

### Create `apps/app/src/lib/activity.ts`

```ts
import {
  ACTIVITY_KEEP_DAYS,
  ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP,
  ACTIVITY_TABS,
  ActivityNewerResponse,
  ActivityPage,
  ActivitySettings,
  MENTION_TOKEN,
  type ActivityEntry,
  type ActivityTab,
} from "@korbat/contracts";
import { IMAGE_LOST_NOTICE } from "@korbat/rules";
import { ACTIVITY_WORDS } from "./activity-words";
import { api } from "./api";
import { RELEASE_TEXTS, UPLOAD_TEXTS } from "./moderation-words";
import { createNewPosts, type NewPostsClock } from "./new-posts";
import { localDay, postedWhen, timeAgo } from "./time";
import { fill } from "./ui-words";

/**
 * Activity in the app (2d design, sections 5.5.3, 5.7, 5.8, 9.2 and 10.2): the five calls of the activity module, and what
 * the screen does with their answers as pure functions, so the tests can drive them: the tab in the address, the rows
 * with their two headings, the marker of the visit, the newer count's pill, the poll's schedule, the focus after a
 * reload or Load more, and the settings' save once a choice settles. Every time of Activity is the API's string with six
 * fractional digits (ActivityTime): it is kept as it came and compared as a string, never passed through Date, which
 * would cut it to the millisecond and leave the marker short of an entry written later in the same millisecond.
 */

const query = (parts: Record<string, string | undefined>) =>
  Object.entries(parts)
    .filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined)
    .map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${encodeURIComponent(value!)}`)
    .join("&");

/** GET /api/activity and /newer, POST /seen, GET and PUT /settings (9.2). Nothing else asks for Activity, anywhere. */
export const activityApi = {
  page: (tab: ActivityTab, cursor?: string) => api(`/api/activity?${query({ tab, cursor })}`, { schema: ActivityPage }),
  newer: (tab: ActivityTab, since?: string) => api(`/api/activity/newer?${query({ tab, since })}`, { schema: ActivityNewerResponse }),
  seen: (at: string) => api("/api/activity/seen", { json: { at } }),
  settings: () => api("/api/activity/settings", { schema: ActivitySettings }),
  saveSettings: (settings: ActivitySettings) => api("/api/activity/settings", { method: "PUT", json: settings, schema: ActivitySettings }),
};

/** The tab the address names (`/activity?tab=conversations`), so a reload keeps it; anything else is All. */
export function activityTab(param: string | string[] | undefined): ActivityTab {
  const named = Array.isArray(param) ? param[0] : param;
  return ACTIVITY_TABS.find((tab) => tab === named) ?? "all";
}

/** The pill's words: "1 new", "{n} new", and "20+ new" from the count's cap. */
export function activityPill(count: number): string {
  if (count >= ACTIVITY_NEWER_CAP) return ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.pill.many"];
  return count === 1 ? ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.pill.one"] : fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.pill"], { n: count });
}

/**
 * Entries marked new against the visit's marker: the first page's `seenAt`, which the screen keeps while it is open, since
 * the marker it sends after that page would make every later page's entries old. Null, before the first visit, is new.
 */
export function markForVisit(items: ActivityEntry[], seenAt: string | null): ActivityEntry[] {
  return items.map((entry) => ({ ...entry, new: seenAt === null || entry.at > seenAt }));
}

/** The seen marker to send after the first page: its newest entry's time, and only when something on it was new (5.7). */
export function seenToSend(page: ActivityPage): string | null {
  return page.items.some((entry) => entry.new) ? page.items[0]!.at : null;
}

export type ActivityRow =
  | { kind: "entry"; key: string; entry: ActivityEntry }
  | { kind: "heading"; key: string; heading: "new" | "earlier" }
  | { kind: "skeleton"; key: string; index: number }
  | { kind: "empty"; key: "empty" }
  | { kind: "error"; key: "error"; message: string }
  | { kind: "loadMore"; key: "loadMore"; busy: boolean }
  | { kind: "loadMoreError"; key: "loadMoreError"; message: string }
  | { kind: "end"; key: "end" };

export interface ActivityRowsInput {
  items: ActivityEntry[];
  status: "loading" | "ready" | "error";
  error: string | null;
  cursor: string | null;
  loadingMore: boolean;
  moreError: string | null;
}

/**
 * The list's rows (10.2): skeletons, the error or the empty state; else the entries, the h2 "New since you last looked"
 * above the first new one and "Earlier" above the first older one, both only when something is new; then Load more, a
 * failed page's sentence, or the end, which names the days korbat keeps.
 */
export function activityRows(input: ActivityRowsInput): ActivityRow[] {
  if (input.status === "loading") return [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((index) => ({ kind: "skeleton", key: `skeleton-${index}`, index }));
  if (input.status === "error") return [{ kind: "error", key: "error", message: input.error ?? "" }];
  if (input.items.length === 0) return [{ kind: "empty", key: "empty" }];
  const rows: ActivityRow[] = [];
  const anyNew = input.items.some((entry) => entry.new);
  let earlier = false;
  input.items.forEach((entry, index) => {
    if (anyNew && index === 0 && entry.new) rows.push({ kind: "heading", key: "heading-new", heading: "new" });
    if (anyNew && !entry.new && !earlier) {
      earlier = true;
      rows.push({ kind: "heading", key: "heading-earlier", heading: "earlier" });
    }
    rows.push({ kind: "entry", key: entry.key, entry });
  });
  if (input.moreError) rows.push({ kind: "loadMoreError", key: "loadMoreError", message: input.moreError });
  else if (input.cursor !== null) rows.push({ kind: "loadMore", key: "loadMore", busy: input.loadingMore });
  else rows.push({ kind: "end", key: "end" });
  return rows;
}

/** Where the focus goes after the pill or a refresh: the list's first entry. */
export function firstEntryKey(rows: ActivityRow[]): string | null {
  return rows.find((row) => row.kind === "entry")?.key ?? null;
}

/** Where the focus goes after Load more: the first entry the page brought, the one after the `before` already shown. */
export function firstLoadedKey(before: number, items: ActivityEntry[]): string | null {
  return items[before]?.key ?? null;
}

/**
 * A focus that waits for its row (10.2): `attempt` is tried at once and every 50 ms until it says the focus landed, for
 * at most 5 s. The list draws its rows in batches, so on a slow device the entry the pill or Load more names may not be
 * drawn yet when the page arrives; trying once would leave a keyboard user on the control they pressed. The answer
 * cancels the tries, for a newer focus request or a list that goes.
 */
export function retryFocus(attempt: () => boolean, everyMs = 50, withinMs = 5000): () => void {
  const deadline = Date.now() + withinMs;
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  const next = () => {
    timer = null;
    if (attempt() || Date.now() >= deadline) return;
    timer = setTimeout(next, everyMs);
  };
  timer = setTimeout(next, 0);
  return () => {
    if (timer !== null) clearTimeout(timer);
    timer = null;
  };
}

/** An entry's line (10.10): who did what, the follows of a day by up to two names and the count, and the notices' words. */
export function entryLine(entry: ActivityEntry): string {
  if (entry.type === "post") return fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS[`activity.${entry.kind}`], { name: entry.post.author.displayName });
  if (entry.type === "follows") {
    const [first, second] = entry.actors;
    if (entry.count === 1) return fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.follow.one"], { name: first!.displayName });
    if (entry.count === 2 && second) return fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.follow.two"], { name: first!.displayName, other: second.displayName });
    return fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.follow.many"], { name: first!.displayName, n: entry.count - 1 });
  }
  const day = entry.postCreatedAt === null ? "" : localDay(entry.postCreatedAt);
  if (entry.kind === "release") return RELEASE_TEXTS.entry;
  if (entry.kind === "upload") return UPLOAD_TEXTS.entry;
  if (entry.kind === "lost") return IMAGE_LOST_NOTICE.mail(day);
  return entry.target === "post" ? fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.decision.post"], { date: day }) : ACTIVITY_WORDS[`activity.decision.${entry.target}`];
}

/** When, as the entry's name says it: "3h ago", "just now", "on 12/10/2026". */
export function activityWhen(at: string): string {
  return timeAgo(at) === "just now" ? timeAgo(at) : postedWhen(at);
}

/** An entry's accessible name (10.2): its line and its time, with "New, " first while it is new. */
export function entryName(entry: ActivityEntry): string {
  return fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS[entry.new ? "activity.entry.newName" : "activity.entry.name"], { line: entryLine(entry), time: activityWhen(entry.at) });
}

/** The end of the list, which names the days an entry is kept. */
export const activityEnd = (): string => fill(ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.end"], { days: ACTIVITY_KEEP_DAYS });

/** Whether the composer's text names a handle (4.5, 10.3): a fresh copy of the global token, so no place is shared. */
export function hasMention(text: string): boolean {
  return new RegExp(MENTION_TOKEN.source).test(text);
}

/** Whether the screen may ask for newer entries: on screen, the page visible, and its first page in (5.8). */
export function activityPollActive(state: { focused: boolean; visible: boolean; ready: boolean }): boolean {
  return state.focused && state.visible && state.ready;
}

/** The feed's schedule (lib/new-posts.ts): 30 s of active time after the screen opens, then 60 s after each answer. */
export function createActivityPoll(ask: () => Promise<unknown>): NewPostsClock {
  return createNewPosts(ask);
}

const same = (a: ActivitySettings, b: ActivitySettings) => a.replies === b.replies && a.mentions === b.mentions && a.quotes === b.quotes && a.follows === b.follows;

/**
 * Settings, Activity's save (10.8): a choice is sent once it has been still for 800 ms, or at once when the focus leaves
 * its group, so arrowing across a group sends one request and shows one toast; a choice back at the saved value sends
 * nothing; a refused save hands the saved value back for the rollback. Saves go one after another, never side by side.
 */
export function createSettingsSaver(options: {
  initial: ActivitySettings;
  save: (next: ActivitySettings) => Promise<ActivitySettings>;
  onSaved: (saved: ActivitySettings) => void;
  onFailed: (saved: ActivitySettings) => void;
  delayMs?: number;
}) {
  let saved = options.initial;
  let pending: ActivitySettings | null = null;
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  let chain: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
  const flush = () => {
    if (timer !== null) clearTimeout(timer);
    timer = null;
    const next = pending;
    pending = null;
    if (next === null) return;
    chain = chain.then(async () => {
      if (same(next, saved)) return;
      try {
        saved = await options.save(next);
        options.onSaved(saved);
      } catch {
        options.onFailed(saved);
      }
    });
  };
  return {
    choose(next: ActivitySettings) {
      pending = next;
      if (timer !== null) clearTimeout(timer);
      timer = setTimeout(flush, options.delayMs ?? 800);
    },
    leave: flush,
    dispose() {
      if (timer !== null) clearTimeout(timer);
      timer = null;
    },
  };
}
```

### Create `apps/app/src/lib/avatar.ts`

```ts
import type { AvatarCrop, AvatarView, MediaStatusResponse, UploadResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ApiError } from "./api";
import { AVATAR_WORDS } from "./settings-words";
import { fill } from "./ui-words";

/**
 * The avatar picker's logic (2d design, decision 14, sections 7.2, 7.3, 7.7 and 10.5), as pure functions the picker on
 * Settings, Profile calls and the tests drive: the choices of the part to keep by the chosen image's shape, the preview's
 * position and name, the upload, its processing and the setting of the picture, and where the focus goes after each.
 */

export type AvatarShape = "square" | "portrait" | "landscape";

export function avatarShape(width: number, height: number): AvatarShape {
  return width === height ? "square" : width < height ? "portrait" : "landscape";
}

/** One choice of "Which part to keep": its words, the crop the worker cuts, and the preview's position over the file. */
export interface CropChoice {
  label: string;
  crop: AvatarCrop;
  position: "top" | "center" | "bottom" | "left" | "right";
}

/**
 * The three parts along the longer side (decision 14): Top, Middle, Bottom for a portrait and Left, Middle, Right for a
 * landscape, as the worker's start, centre and end; a square has nothing to choose. Each moves the preview's position,
 * so the preview is the square the worker will keep.
 */
export function cropChoices(shape: AvatarShape): CropChoice[] {
  if (shape === "square") return [];
  const portrait = shape === "portrait";
  return [
    { label: portrait ? AVATAR_WORDS.top : AVATAR_WORDS.left, crop: "start", position: portrait ? "top" : "left" },
    { label: AVATAR_WORDS.middle, crop: "centre", position: "center" },
    { label: portrait ? AVATAR_WORDS.bottom : AVATAR_WORDS.right, crop: "end", position: portrait ? "bottom" : "right" },
  ];
}

/** The preview's name: the part kept, or the plain name for a square. */
export function previewName(choice: CropChoice | null): string {
  return choice ? fill(AVATAR_WORDS.previewPart, { part: choice.label }) : AVATAR_WORDS.preview;
}

export type AvatarOutcome = { status: "set"; avatar: AvatarView | null } | { status: "refused"; refusalId: string } | { status: "failed" } | { status: "reset" } | { status: "error"; error: unknown };

/** The calls the sequence makes: lib/social.ts's, or a test's fakes. */
export interface AvatarClient {
  uploadMedia: (file: Blob, avatar: { crop: AvatarCrop }) => Promise<UploadResponse>;
  mediaStatus: (id: string) => Promise<MediaStatusResponse>;
  setAvatar: (mediaId: string) => Promise<{ avatar: AvatarView | null }>;
}

/** How often the upload's state is asked, and for how long at most, as the composer does (useImageUploads). */
const POLL_MS = 1000;
const GIVE_UP_MS = 6 * 60_000;
const pause = () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, POLL_MS));

/**
 * "Use this picture" (10.5): uploads the file as kind=avatar with the crop ("uploading"), asks its state until it is
 * settled ("processing"), and sets a ready one as the account's picture. A refused upload is never set and names its
 * refusal, whose notice the "Why" link opens; a failed one is failed; the picture a moderator reset less than 30 days ago
 * is refused by PUT /api/me/avatar's avatar_reset (7.7); any other refusal is handed back as it came.
 */
export async function sendAvatar(client: AvatarClient, file: Blob, crop: AvatarCrop, onStep: (step: "uploading" | "processing") => void, wait: () => Promise<void> = pause): Promise<AvatarOutcome> {
  try {
    onStep("uploading");
    const sent = await client.uploadMedia(file, { crop });
    onStep("processing");
    const deadline = Date.now() + GIVE_UP_MS;
    for (;;) {
      const state = await client.mediaStatus(sent.id);
      if (state.status === "refused") return { status: "refused", refusalId: state.refusalId };
      if (state.status === "failed") return { status: "failed" };
      if (state.status === "ready") break;
      if (Date.now() > deadline) return { status: "failed" };
      await wait();
    }
    return { status: "set", avatar: (await client.setAvatar(sent.id)).avatar };
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ApiError && error.code === "avatar_reset") return { status: "reset" };
    return { status: "error", error };
  }
}

/**
 * Where the focus goes (10.5): after a picture is set, to "Choose another picture"; after Cancel or a removal, to "Choose
 * a picture"; after a refusal, a failure or any error, to the error line, which says why with its "Why" link next.
 */
export function pickerFocus(event: AvatarOutcome | "cancel" | "removed"): "change" | "choose" | "error" {
  if (event === "cancel" || event === "removed") return "choose";
  return event.status === "set" ? "change" : "error";
}
```

### Replace `README.md` (whole file)

````markdown
# korbat

Pseudonymous social platform with a narrow public rulebook and transparent moderation. Self-hosted.

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-korbat-design.md`
- Accounts and sessions (sub-project 1a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-identity-auth-1a-design.md`
- Posting and feed (sub-project 2a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-posting-feed-2a-design.md`
- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/`

## Dev quick start
```bash
pnpm install
node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs                # creates or completes infra/.env, apps/api/.env, apps/app/.env, apps/worker/.env and apps/importer/.env, and derives apps/api/.env.test; values are random and never printed
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis counts mailpit   # dev host ports 55432, 56379, 56380, 51025, 58025 (movable: DEV_*_PORT in infra/.env)
pnpm --filter @korbat/api dev               # http://localhost:3000/api/health; reads apps/api/.env
pnpm --filter @korbat/worker dev            # the image worker; reads apps/worker/.env and works on .data/media
pnpm --filter @korbat/importer dev          # the importer of archives (3b); reads apps/importer/.env and works on .data/import, which the API's IMPORT_*_DIR name too
pnpm --filter @korbat/app web               # http://localhost:8081
pnpm --filter @korbat/admin dev             # the staff console at http://localhost:8090 (never 127.0.0.1); forwards /api/staff/* to the API above
```

Emails sent in development (sign-in codes, new-device alerts, lockout notices) land in Mailpit at http://localhost:58025. Locally the web app uses Cloudflare's always-pass Turnstile test key, so the human check never blocks you.

The data services are PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey (the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, still under the service name `redis`, on its own volume `valkeydata`: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into the old `redisdata` volume, which held only transient state and can be removed with `docker volume rm`). Valkey needs the password from `infra/.env`; `gen-dev-env` writes it into the API's `REDIS_URL` too, so an older `.env` is fixed by running it again. The recipients' count (the day's key and the counting sketches of the transparency page) lives in a Valkey of its own, the service `counts`, which writes nothing to disk: no append-only file, no snapshot, no volume. A restart of `counts` loses the running month's count, which then reads "not recorded"; nothing else is kept there. It takes the same password, and the API reads it as `COUNTS_URL`, which Compose sets.

korbat once ran MinIO and never used it. Images live on two Docker volumes instead, `media-uploads` and `media-store`. If an old stack left a `korbat_miniodata` volume behind, `docker volume rm korbat_miniodata` removes it.

## Tests
```bash
pnpm test                                     # unit tests of every package
node scripts/test-db.mjs                      # creates or migrates the korbat_test database; run it again after adding a migration
pnpm --filter @korbat/api test:integration    # needs postgres, redis and mailpit up
```

Integration tests have their own database, `korbat_test`, and their own Redis database, 15. Both are named in `apps/api/.env.test`, which `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` derives from `apps/api/.env`. Every run starts by emptying them, and refuses to start if a URL points anywhere else, so tests never touch development data.

Before they had their own database, the integration suites left accounts, profiles and posts in the development database, and the smoke test still leaves its first account per run, by then a moderator, with one open moderation case on that account's post. To see and remove them:

```bash
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs          # lists test accounts and profiles without an account; deletes nothing
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs --yes    # deletes them with everything they made
```

It only matches emails of the tests' shape, `<word>-<uuid>@korbat.local`, recomputes the counters of kept profiles and posts they touched, and refuses to run unless `API_APP_ORIGIN` in `infra/.env` is a localhost origin. It keeps an account that holds a staff key or that the moderation record names (one that decided anything, one on either side of a staff link, the subject of a case that a decision or a reveal names), and counts it as kept; every other case about a deleted account or one of its posts is deleted with it, the smoke test's open case included.

## Full stack
```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d --build   # http://localhost:8080, and the staff console at http://localhost:8090
node scripts/smoke-auth-stack.mjs --base http://localhost:8080 --console http://localhost:8090 --mailpit http://localhost:58025 --terms draft-2026-09 -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

The smoke test first checks the staff console's site: its page carries the console's own policy and is never stored, and the staff API answers there (401 without a session) and nowhere else (Caddy's own 404 on the app's site); the console's case routes (the overview, the queue, a case, the appeals) answer the same two ways, and the console's site refuses the app's own moderation routes with a 404 of its own. It then signs up a throwaway account through Caddy, reads its code from Mailpit, posts and reads the post back from the public Latest timeline. It uploads a JPEG carrying a GPS position, posts it, and checks that the served file is a fresh WebP without metadata, that a symlink planted in the store from inside the worker gets a 404, and that deleting the post removes the image from disk. It checks the worker's isolation, then imports a Mastodon archive the script builds: sent in chunks through Caddy, read by the real importer in its isolation, confirmed, its four posts read on the profile's Imported tab and in no feed, and removed again with Remove imported posts. Then it grants the account a staff role with the CLI and checks that its session was revoked. A second throwaway account edits its bio, changes its handle, reports the first account's post under a rule, finds that report undecided in its own list and in its export's member `moderation`, followed by its imports (none), and deletes itself. Last, signed out, a notice that the same post is illegal is taken with the human check: it answers a reference and a token, the status page opens with that token, the receipt arrives in Mailpit, and the token in the receipt's link opens the same page. Nothing in it decides the case, since a decision needs a staff key: every run leaves one open case in lane 2 on the first account's post. One network can run it five times an hour and five times a day, since its two sign-ups count against the hourly sign-up limit, its signed-out notice against the limits of reports sent without an account, and its import against the imports started from one address in a day.

After every sharp upgrade, add `--worst-case`: it also uploads flat-colour files at the pixel caps (48 MP 16-bit interlaced PNG, 48 MP progressive JPEG, 48 MP GIF, 16 MP AVIF), expects each to be ready without the worker being OOM-killed or restarted, and prints the worker's memory peak.

Caddy listens on 8080 inside its container as its own user, proxies `/api` to the API and serves the web app with the page's security headers; `index.html` is revalidated on every load and the hashed bundles are cached for a year. On 8090 it serves the staff console under the console's own policy and proxies only `/api/staff/*`, which the app's site refuses. On 8091 it serves the phones' push site: only the two alert topics' subscriptions reach ntfy, and every other path is Caddy's own 404. The compose file keeps cloudflared, Caddy, the API and the data services on separate networks, so cloudflared reaches only Caddy and Caddy only the API and ntfy.
````
