```tsx
interface AppShellProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  /** A control floating over a phone's column, bottom right. */
  floating?: ReactNode;
  /** The phone's compose button on this screen (7.2: Home, a profile and Bookmarks), for a signed-in reader. */
  compose?: boolean;
  /** What New post does here instead of opening the sheet: Home opens and focuses its own card from 768 px. */
  onNewPost?: () => void;
}

export function AppShell({ children, floating, compose = false, onNewPost }: AppShellProps) {
  const kind = useLayout();
  return (
    <ShellScrollProvider phone={kind === "phone"}>
      <Shell kind={kind} floating={floating} compose={compose} onNewPost={onNewPost}>
        {children}
      </Shell>
    </ShellScrollProvider>
  );
}

function Shell({ kind, children, floating, compose, onNewPost }: { kind: LayoutKind } & AppShellProps) {
  const { state } = useSession();
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
  const scroll = useShellScroll();
  const main = useRef<View>(null);
  const signedIn = state.status === "signed-in";
  const handle = signedIn ? state.me.profile?.handle : undefined;
  // 3e (design, section 9.1): above every signed-in screen while /me's standing holds a measure.
  const banner = signedIn ? <StandingBanner standing={state.me.standing} /> : null;
  const phone = kind === "phone";
  const items = navItems(state.status, handle, phone);
  const newPost = signedIn ? (onNewPost ?? openNewPost) : undefined;
  // The phone's floating control: the screen's own, or the compose button where the screen asks for it.
  const shownFloating = floating ?? (compose && newPost ? <ComposeButton onPress={newPost} /> : null);
  const hasFloating = shownFloating !== undefined && shownFloating !== null && shownFloating !== false;

  // Toasts on a phone screen with the compose button sit above it (section 5.4); the Toaster lives outside the screen.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!phone || !hasFloating) return;
    setComposeButtonShown(true);
    return () => setComposeButtonShown(false);
  }, [phone, hasFloating]);

  // The skip link's target: the main column itself takes the focus, so the next Tab starts inside it.
  const focusMain = () => (main.current as unknown as { focus?: () => void } | null)?.focus?.();
  const nav: NavProps = { items, pathname, onHomeAgain: (event) => softReset(event, scroll) };

  const column = (
    <View ref={main} role="main" nativeID="main" tabIndex={-1} className={cn("flex-1", FOCUS_RING_INSET)}>
      <OfflineBanner />
      {banner}
      <View className="flex-1">{children}</View>
    </View>
  );

  if (phone) {
    return (
      <View {...layoutData(kind)} className="flex-1 bg-surface">
        <SkipLink onSkip={focusMain} />
        {/* The tab bar comes before the column in the page, after the skip link, and is drawn below it. */}
        <View className="flex-1 flex-col-reverse">
          <TabBar {...nav} />
          {column}
        </View>
        {hasFloating ? (
          // 16 px from the right, and 16 px above the tab bar and the bottom safe area (section 7.2).
          <View pointerEvents="box-none" style={{ position: "absolute", right: 16, bottom: 56 + insets.bottom + 16 }}>
            {shownFloating}
          </View>
        ) : null}
      </View>
    );
  }

  const context = kind === "desktop" || kind === "wide";
  const navWidth = kind === "wide" ? COLUMNS.nav : COLUMNS.rail;
  // The columns sit together, 24 px apart with a line-low rule on each side of the main column: 1,208 px at wide.
  const together = navWidth + COLUMNS.gap + COLUMNS.timeline + 2 + COLUMNS.gap + COLUMNS.context;
  const timeline = (
    <View className="min-w-0 flex-1 border-x border-line-low" style={{ maxWidth: COLUMNS.timeline + 2 }}>
      {column}
    </View>
  );
  return (
    <View {...layoutData(kind)} className="flex-1 flex-row justify-center bg-surface">
      <SkipLink onSkip={focusMain} />
      {context ? (
        <View className="w-full flex-row" style={{ maxWidth: together, gap: COLUMNS.gap }}>
          <SideNav {...nav} full={kind === "wide"} newPost={newPost} />
          {timeline}
          <ContextColumn />
        </View>
      ) : (
        // A tablet: the rail at the left edge and the column centred in the rest.
        <View className="w-full flex-row">
          <SideNav {...nav} full={false} newPost={newPost} />
          <View className="min-w-0 flex-1 flex-row justify-center">
            {timeline}
          </View>
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Pressable, View } from "react-native";
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { IMPORT_WORDS } from "@/lib/import-words";
import { CASES_WORDS } from "@/lib/moderation-words";
import { ACTIVITY_SETTINGS_WORDS } from "@/lib/settings-words";
import { UI_WORDS } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";
import type { IconName } from "./icons";
import { FOCUS_RING, HOVER_WASH } from "./kit/interaction";
import { Text } from "./kit/Text";

export type SettingsPage = "appearance" | "activity" | "security" | "privacy" | "profile" | "account" | "import" | "cases";

/**
 * The settings pages in their order, with their names and icons (UI design, sections 4.7 and 8.8): Appearance first
 * (UI Task 8, the owner's ruling 10), so the page a newcomer looks for comes first, in this row and in the Settings
 * index (app/settings/index.tsx), which lists the same pages as rows.
 */
export const SETTINGS_PAGES: { page: SettingsPage; label: string; icon: IconName; row?: string; hint?: string }[] = [
  { page: "appearance", label: UI_WORDS["appearance.nav"], icon: "appearance" },
  // 2d (10.8): Activity after Appearance, with its hint under the index's row.
  { page: "activity", label: ACTIVITY_SETTINGS_WORDS.nav, icon: "activity", hint: ACTIVITY_SETTINGS_WORDS.hint },
  { page: "security", label: UI_WORDS["settings.security"], icon: "security" },
  { page: "privacy", label: UI_WORDS["settings.privacy"], icon: "privacy" },
  { page: "profile", label: UI_WORDS["settings.profile"], icon: "edit-profile" },
  { page: "account", label: UI_WORDS["settings.account"], icon: "account" },
  // 3b (design, section 10.1): Import after Account in this row, and "Import posts" as the Settings index's row (`row`).
  { page: "import", label: IMPORT_WORDS["import.nav"], icon: "import", row: IMPORT_WORDS["import.title"] },
  // The decisions about the account and the reports it sent (3c design, section 9); its screens are the folder settings/cases.
  { page: "cases", label: CASES_WORDS.nav, icon: "cases" },
];

/**
 * The row of links between the settings screens, shown by every one of them under its title but the index, which is the
 * list itself. Each link is a real anchor (expo-router's Link), so the keyboard can follow it. The screen names itself
 * through `current` instead of the row asking the router for the path, which also lets a test render the row on its own.
 * Appearance shows the row only to a signed-in reader, since the others need an account.
 *
 * On the tokens (UI design, sections 4.8 and 7.1): each link a 44 px pill that wraps rather than clipping its word, the
 * current one in the accent wash with its label in body-strong and an accent underline beneath it, a shape mark that
 * does not rely on the colour; the others ink-medium, with the hover wash under a fine pointer.
 */
export function SettingsNav({ current }: { current: SettingsPage }) {
  return (
    <View role="navigation" aria-label={UI_WORDS["settings.nav"]} className="mt-3 flex-row flex-wrap gap-1">
      {SETTINGS_PAGES.map(({ page, label }) => (
        <Link key={page} href={`/settings/${page}`} asChild>
          <Pressable
            aria-current={page === current ? "page" : undefined}
            className={cn("min-h-[44px] justify-center rounded-full px-3 active:bg-surface-2", page === current ? "bg-accent-wash" : HOVER_WASH, FOCUS_RING)}
          >
            <Text variant={page === current ? "body-strong" : "body"} tone={page === current ? "high" : "medium"} className={page === current ? "underline decoration-accent web:decoration-2 web:underline-offset-4" : undefined}>
              {label}
            </Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      ))}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```ts
import type { Tone } from "./kit/Text";

/**
 * The closed list of icons korbat draws (UI design, section 4.7), each mapped to its Lucide 1.55.0 export name. The
 * names are strings, so this file imports neither icon package: kit/Icon.web.tsx imports the components from
 * lucide-react and kit/Icon.tsx from lucide-react-native, each as a Record<IconName, ...>, so tsc refuses a name that
 * either side lacks, only listed icons are bundled, and the web export and the unit tests never load the native set.
 * restricted and hidden share EyeOff: not shown to others, as on a hidden image (Lucide's Ban, a prohibition sign, is
 * not used). Trash2 is Lucide's own name, which 1.55.0 exports as an alias of Trash.
 */
export const ICONS = {
  home: "House",
  bookmarks: "Bookmark",
  profile: "CircleUser",
  settings: "Settings",
  compose: "SquarePen",
  reply: "MessageCircle",
  repost: "Repeat2",
  quote: "Quote",
  like: "Heart",
  more: "Ellipsis",
  "who-sees": "Eye",
  "copy-link": "Link",
  delete: "Trash2",
  report: "Flag",
  close: "X",
  back: "ArrowLeft",
  newer: "ArrowUp",
  previous: "ChevronLeft",
  next: "ChevronRight",
  "add-image": "ImagePlus",
  error: "CircleAlert",
  offline: "WifiOff",
  done: "CircleCheck",
  review: "Clock",
  restricted: "EyeOff",
  verified: "BadgeCheck",
  explore: "Compass",
  hidden: "EyeOff",
  security: "Shield",
  privacy: "Lock",
  "edit-profile": "UserPen",
  account: "UserCog",
  cases: "Scale",
  appearance: "Palette",
  "sign-in": "LogIn",
  passkey: "KeyRound",
  external: "ExternalLink",
  info: "Info",
  retry: "RotateCw",
  /** 3b (design, section 10.1): Settings' Import posts and the provenance label of an imported post. */
  import: "Import",
  /** 2d (decision 24, 10.1): the nav's Activity item; it never carries a dot or a number. */
  activity: "Bell",
} as const;

export type IconName = keyof typeof ICONS;

/** The sizes an icon is drawn at: 24 in the nav and tab bar, 20 in post actions, buttons and rows, 16 inline with meta text, 14 in chips. */
export type IconSize = 14 | 16 | 20 | 24;

/** What Icon takes, the same on web and native (kit/Icon.web.tsx and kit/Icon.tsx). */
export interface IconProps {
  name: IconName;
  /** Defaults to 20, the size of post actions, buttons and rows. */
  size?: IconSize;
  /** The colour, as Text's tones; ink-high by default. */
  tone?: Tone;
  /** Filled with its own colour: Heart and Bookmark when on. */
  filled?: boolean;
  /** Stroke 2.25 instead of 1.75: the current nav item, a reposted Repeat2. */
  strong?: boolean;
}
```

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode, type Ref } from "react";
import { Pressable, View } from "react-native";
import { Link, type Href } from "expo-router";
import type { ImportView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { FOCUS_RING } from "@/components/kit/interaction";
import { ProgressBar } from "@/components/kit/ProgressBar";
import { Sheet } from "@/components/kit/Sheet";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { Button, ErrorText, Notice } from "@/components/ui";
import { IMPORT_WORDS, ruleWords } from "@/lib/import-words";
import { formatCount, importErrorMessage, imports } from "@/lib/imports";
import { UI_WORDS, fill } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";

/**
 * The parts every view of an import shares (3b design, sections 10.1 and 10.5), and the progress of an import that
 * prepares, publishes or removes its posts.
 */

/**
 * The level-2 heading each state's view starts with (10.1). It can take the focus (tabIndex -1), so the screen moves the
 * focus to it when a change of state removed the element that held it; it shows the kit's ring then.
 */
export function StateHeading({ children, headingRef, variant = "display-3" }: { children: string; headingRef?: Ref<View>; variant?: "display-3" | "title" }) {
  return (
    // The title variant heads the preview's first card, inside its padding; the others start a view.
    <Text as="h2" variant={variant} className={cn(variant === "title" ? undefined : "mt-6", "self-start rounded-sm", FOCUS_RING)} {...({ ref: headingRef, tabIndex: -1 } as object)}>
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}

/** A sentence of a view, in ink-medium unless it is the view's news. */
export function Line({ children, tone = "medium" }: { children: string; tone?: "high" | "medium" }) {
  return (
    <Text tone={tone} className="mt-3">
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}

/** A real link inside a view: accent-ink and underlined, 44 px tall, as TextLink is but at the start of its line. */
export function ViewLink({ label, href }: { label: string; href: Href }) {
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable className={cn("mt-3 min-h-[44px] justify-center self-start rounded-control active:opacity-70", FOCUS_RING)}>
        <Text tone="accent" className="underline web:underline-offset-2">
          {label}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  );
}

/**
 * A question asked once in a Sheet before an action that cannot be taken back (10.3: Cancel import; 10.5: Stop import,
 * Remove imported posts): the question names the dialog, the action in danger, the way back as a second button. A
 * refusal is said under them; the sheet stays open for another try.
 */
export function AskSheet({
  open,
  title,
  description,
  confirm,
  keep,
  busy,
  error,
  onConfirm,
  onClose,
  onClosed,
}: {
  open: boolean;
  title: string;
  /** 2d (10.5): a sentence under the question, as Sheet's description (the avatar's removal says what goes). */
  description?: string;
  confirm: string;
  keep: string;
  busy: boolean;
  error: string | null;
  onConfirm: () => void;
  onClose: () => void;
  onClosed: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Sheet open={open} onClose={onClose} onClosed={onClosed} title={title} description={description}>
      <View className="px-5 pb-4">
        <ErrorText message={error} />
        <View className="flex-row flex-wrap gap-x-2">
          <Button label={confirm} tone="danger" full={false} busy={busy} onPress={onConfirm} />
          <Button label={keep} tone="secondary" full={false} onPress={onClose} />
        </View>
      </View>
    </Sheet>
  );
}

/**
 * An action asked once (AskSheet) behind a secondary button, which then answers the import as it now stands: the view's
 * Cancel import, Stop import and Remove imported posts. `onAsk` runs as the sheet opens (the warning haptic of Remove).
 */
export function AskedAction({
  label,
  question,
  confirm,
  keep,
  act,
  onView,
  onAsk,
}: {
  label: string;
  question: string;
  confirm: string;
  keep: string;
  act: () => Promise<ImportView>;
  onView: (next: ImportView) => void;
  onAsk?: () => void;
}) {
  const [sheet, setSheet] = useState({ mounted: false, open: false });
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const run = async () => {
    if (busy) return;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const next = await act();
      setSheet({ mounted: true, open: false });
      onView(next);
    } catch (err) {
      setError(importErrorMessage(err, { during: "act" }));
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  };
  return (
    <>
      <Button
        label={label}
        tone="secondary"
        full={false}
        onPress={() => {
          onAsk?.();
          setError(null);
          setSheet({ mounted: true, open: true });
        }}
      />
      {sheet.mounted ? (
        <AskSheet
          open={sheet.open}
          title={question}
          confirm={confirm}
          keep={keep}
          busy={busy}
          error={error}
          onConfirm={() => void run()}
          onClose={() => setSheet({ mounted: true, open: false })}
          onClosed={() => setSheet({ mounted: false, open: false })}
        />
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}

/** A phase's bar with its words above it as its value text ("Publishing posts: 800 of 1,240"). */
function Phase({ words, done, total }: { words: string; done: number; total: number }) {
  const text = fill(words, { done: formatCount(done), total: formatCount(total) });
  return (
    <View className="mt-4 gap-2">
      <Text variant="body-strong">{text}</Text>
      <ProgressBar label={text} value={done} max={total} valueText={text} />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * Preparing and publishing (10.5): a bar per phase, You can leave this page, and Stop import, asked once; while the author
 * is suspended, the notice that the import is paused (its bars stand still, since nothing moves). Removing (10.5): the
 * bar of the posts removed, and when korbat's staff ended the import, their sentence with the link to the decision (8.7).
 */
export function ImportProgress({ view, headingRef, onView }: { view: ImportView; headingRef?: Ref<View>; onView: (next: ImportView) => void }) {
  const { progress } = view;
  if (view.status === "undoing") {
    return (
      <View>
        <StateHeading headingRef={headingRef}>{IMPORT_WORDS["import.state.undoing"]}</StateHeading>
        {view.endedByStaff !== null ? <StaffEnded view={view} /> : null}
        <Phase words={IMPORT_WORDS["import.removing"]} done={progress.postsRemoved} total={progress.postsPublished} />
      </View>
    );
  }
  return (
    <View>
      <StateHeading headingRef={headingRef}>{IMPORT_WORDS[view.status === "preparing" ? "import.state.preparing" : "import.state.publishing"]}</StateHeading>
      {view.paused ? <Notice message={IMPORT_WORDS["import.paused"]} /> : null}
      {view.status === "preparing" ? <Phase words={IMPORT_WORDS["import.preparing"]} done={progress.imagesSettled} total={progress.imagesTotal} /> : null}
      <Phase words={IMPORT_WORDS["import.publishing"]} done={progress.postsPublished} total={progress.postsTotal} />
      <Line>{IMPORT_WORDS["import.leave"]}</Line>
      <View className="mt-2">
        <AskedAction
          label={IMPORT_WORDS["import.stop"]}
          question={IMPORT_WORDS["import.stop.ask"]}
          confirm={IMPORT_WORDS["import.stop"]}
          keep={IMPORT_WORDS["import.stop.keep"]}
          act={() => imports.stop(view.id)}
          onView={onView}
        />
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

/** korbat's staff ended the import (8.7): their rule, and the decision, which can be appealed, under the person's Cases. */
export function StaffEnded({ view }: { view: ImportView }): ReactNode {
  return (
    <View>
      <Line tone="high">{fill(IMPORT_WORDS["import.endedByStaff"], { rule: ruleWords(view.endedByStaff ?? "") })}</Line>
      {view.staffDecisionId !== null ? <ViewLink label={UI_WORDS["reach.decision"]} href={`/settings/cases/${view.staffDecisionId}`} /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { View } from "react-native";
import { Image } from "expo-image";
import type { AvatarView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { API_BASE } from "@/lib/api";
import { Text, fontVariation, type TextVariant } from "./Text";

/**
 * An account's picture (UI design, section 6.5, decision 22): without an uploaded picture, a monogram, the first grapheme
 * of the display name, ink-medium on surface-2 inside a 1 px line-low ring, with no hue, since colour in korbat means
 * action or status and a coloured disc per account would mean neither. 2d (10.4): with `src`, the account's picture in
 * the same disc, ring and size, through expo-image with no transition, so nothing moves; the monogram stays when there is
 * none or the file fails to load. It is decoration, hidden from assistive technology: the author link beside it carries
 * the name. 32 and 40 px in rows and cards, 64 px (phones) and 96 px in the profile header.
 */
export type AvatarSize = 32 | 40 | 64 | 96;

/**
 * The letter's variant: the text face at 700 in the small discs, Fraunces at the large ones, where the letter is above
 * 22 px, so the profile header's name and disc share the display face.
 */
const LETTER: Record<AvatarSize, TextVariant> = { 32: "body-strong", 40: "title", 64: "display-2", 96: "display-1" };

/** Splits text into what a reader sees as characters, where the runtime can; a letter and its accent stay together. */
const segmenter = typeof Intl !== "undefined" && "Segmenter" in Intl ? new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, { granularity: "grapheme" }) : null;

/** The monogram of a display name: its first grapheme, in capitals; nothing for an empty name. */
export function monogram(displayName: string): string {
  const name = displayName.trim();
  if (name === "") return "";
  const first = segmenter ? (segmenter.segment(name)[Symbol.iterator]().next().value?.segment ?? "") : (Array.from(name)[0] ?? "");
  return first.toLocaleUpperCase();
}

/** The file a disc of `size` draws: the 128 px small.webp at 32 and 40 px, the 400 px large.webp at 64 and 96; none after an error. */
export function avatarFile(src: AvatarView | null | undefined, size: AvatarSize, failed: boolean): string | null {
  if (!src || failed) return null;
  return size >= 64 ? src.large : src.small;
}

export function Avatar({ account, size = 40, src }: { account: { id: string; displayName: string }; size?: AvatarSize; src?: AvatarView | null }) {
  const large = size >= 64;
  // A file that fails to load (gone, or withheld since the view was read) gives way to the monogram, in the same place.
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const file = avatarFile(src, size, failed !== null && failed === (src ? src.small + src.large : null));
  return (
    <View aria-hidden className="items-center justify-center overflow-hidden rounded-full border border-line-low bg-surface-2" style={{ width: size, height: size }}>
      {file !== null ? (
        <Image source={{ uri: `${API_BASE}${file}` }} transition={0} contentFit="cover" style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }} onError={() => setFailed(src ? src.small + src.large : null)} />
      ) : (
        <Text variant={LETTER[size]} tone="medium" style={large ? fontVariation('"SOFT" 100') : undefined}>
          {monogram(account.displayName)}
        </Text>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import Trash2 from "lucide-react-native/icons/trash";

import UserPen from "lucide-react-native/icons/user-pen";
import WifiOff from "lucide-react-native/icons/wifi-off";

import type { IconName, IconProps } from "@/components/icons";

/**
 * An icon on iOS and Android (UI design, sections 4.7 and 6.3): lucide-react-native over react-native-svg, the same
 * names and version as the web's, hidden from accessibility services; the control around it carries the name. Its
 * colour is the tone's token in the reader's theme.
 *
 * Each icon comes from its own module (the package's `icons/*` export), so the bundle carries these icons and not the
 * whole set its main entry re-exports. 1.55.0 has no module of its own for the alias Trash2, which is Trash.
 */
const COMPONENTS: Record<IconName, LucideIcon> = {
  home: House,
  bookmarks: Bookmark,
  profile: CircleUser,
  settings: Settings,
  compose: SquarePen,
  reply: MessageCircle,
  repost: Repeat2,
  quote: Quote,
  like: Heart,
  more: Ellipsis,
  "who-sees": Eye,
  "copy-link": Link,
  delete: Trash2,
  report: Flag,
  close: X,
  back: ArrowLeft,
  newer: ArrowUp,
  previous: ChevronLeft,
  next: ChevronRight,
  "add-image": ImagePlus,
  error: CircleAlert,
  offline: WifiOff,
  done: CircleCheck,
  review: Clock,
  restricted: EyeOff,
  verified: BadgeCheck,
  explore: Compass,
  hidden: EyeOff,
  security: Shield,
  privacy: Lock,
  "edit-profile": UserPen,
  account: UserCog,
  cases: Scale,
  appearance: Palette,
  "sign-in": LogIn,
  passkey: KeyRound,
  external: ExternalLink,
  info: Info,
  retry: RotateCw,
  import: Import,
  activity: Bell,
};

/** Lucide's 24 px drawing has a stroke of 2; korbat draws 1.75, scaled with the icon, and 2.25 when strong. */
export function Icon({ name, size = 20, tone = "high", filled = false, strong = false }: IconProps) {
  const { colors } = useTheme();
  const Drawn = COMPONENTS[name];
  const color = colors[TONE_TOKEN[tone]];
  return <Drawn size={size} color={color} strokeWidth={strong ? 2.25 : 1.75} fill={filled ? color : "none"} accessible={false} />;
}
```

```tsx
import MessageCircle from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/message-circle.mjs";
import Palette from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/palette.mjs";
import Quote from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/quote.mjs";
import Repeat2 from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/repeat-2.mjs";
import RotateCw from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/rotate-cw.mjs";
import Scale from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/scale.mjs";
import Settings from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/settings.mjs";
import Shield from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/shield.mjs";
import SquarePen from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/square-pen.mjs";
import Trash2 from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/trash-2.mjs";
import UserCog from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/user-cog.mjs";
import UserPen from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/user-pen.mjs";
import WifiOff from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/wifi-off.mjs";
import X from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/x.mjs";
import type { IconName, IconProps } from "@/components/icons";
import { TONE_CLASS } from "./Text";

/**
 * An icon on web (UI design, sections 4.7 and 6.3): lucide-react's plain svg, decoration only, so it is hidden from
 * assistive technology and never takes the focus; the control around it carries the name. Its colour is the tone's
 * class, which the svg's stroke follows as currentColor, so a forced Dark scope recolours it with its text.
 *
 * Each icon comes from its own module. lucide-react's main entry re-exports every icon of the set, and Metro keeps
 * whatever a module re-exports, so a named import from it put the whole set in the web bundle (about 240 KB gzip); only
 * these files are bundled now. The package ships no types for them, so lucide-icons.d.ts types each as a LucideIcon.
 */
const COMPONENTS: Record<IconName, LucideIcon> = {
  home: House,
  bookmarks: Bookmark,
  profile: CircleUser,
  settings: Settings,
  compose: SquarePen,
  reply: MessageCircle,
  repost: Repeat2,
  quote: Quote,
  like: Heart,
  more: Ellipsis,
  "who-sees": Eye,
  "copy-link": Link,
  delete: Trash2,
  report: Flag,
  close: X,
  back: ArrowLeft,
  newer: ArrowUp,
  previous: ChevronLeft,
  next: ChevronRight,
  "add-image": ImagePlus,
  error: CircleAlert,
  offline: WifiOff,
  done: CircleCheck,
  review: Clock,
  restricted: EyeOff,
  verified: BadgeCheck,
  explore: Compass,
  hidden: EyeOff,
  security: Shield,
  privacy: Lock,
  "edit-profile": UserPen,
  account: UserCog,
  cases: Scale,
  appearance: Palette,
  "sign-in": LogIn,
  passkey: KeyRound,
  external: ExternalLink,
  info: Info,
  retry: RotateCw,
  import: Import,
  activity: Bell,
};

/** Lucide's 24 px drawing has a stroke of 2; korbat draws 1.75, scaled with the icon, and 2.25 when strong. */
export function Icon({ name, size = 20, tone = "high", filled = false, strong = false }: IconProps) {
  const Drawn = COMPONENTS[name];
  return (
    <Drawn
      size={size}
      strokeWidth={strong ? 2.25 : 1.75}
      fill={filled ? "currentColor" : "none"}
      className={TONE_CLASS[tone]}
      aria-hidden="true"
      focusable="false"
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { useEffect, useImperativeHandle, useReducer, useRef, useState, type Ref } from "react";
import { Switch, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST, type PostView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ListRow, switchColours } from "@/components/kit/ListRow";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { toast } from "@/components/toast";
import { hasMention } from "@/lib/activity";
import { ACTIVITY_WORDS } from "@/lib/activity-words";
import { errorMessage } from "@/lib/api";
import { createDraftKeeper, draftContext, readDraft } from "@/lib/drafts";
import { useHaptics } from "@/lib/haptics";
import { canPickImages, pickImages } from "@/lib/pick-images";
import { useSession } from "@/lib/session";
import { social } from "@/lib/social";
import { UI_WORDS } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { useTheme } from "@/theme/ThemeProvider";
import { ComposerField } from "./composer/ComposerField";
import { DiscardDialog } from "./composer/DiscardDialog";
import { SendBar } from "./composer/SendBar";
import { composerReducer, composerView, initialComposer, type ComposerKind } from "./composer/state";
import { ComposerImages } from "./ComposerImages";
import { QuoteEmbed } from "./PostCard";
import { useImageUploads } from "./useImageUploads";

/** What sending says, by what was sent (section 5.4): the same name as the button had. */
const SENT: Record<ComposerKind, string> = { post: UI_WORDS["toast.sent.post"], reply: UI_WORDS["toast.sent.reply"], quote: UI_WORDS["toast.sent.quote"] };

/**
 * The toast after sending (UI design, sections 5.4 and 6.15): the sentence names what was sent, and its View opens the
 * new post. It is announced politely; the post's own place is in the sentence, so View is a convenience, not the only way.
 */
export function announceSent(kind: ComposerKind, post: PostView): void {
  toast.show({ message: SENT[kind], action: { label: UI_WORDS["toast.view"], onPress: () => router.push(`/post/${post.id}`) } });
}

/** What a card does with its composer: put the focus back in the field. */
export interface ComposerHandle {
  focus(): void;
}

interface ComposerProps {
  replyTo?: PostView;
  quoteOf?: PostView;
  onPosted?: (post: PostView) => void;
  /** Cancel in the send bar, which a sheet gives: it closes, asking first when there is content. */
  onCancel?: () => void;
  autoFocus?: boolean;
  /** Told whenever the draft gains or loses content, so a sheet can ask before discarding it. */
  onDirtyChange?: (dirty: boolean) => void;
  /** The discard question shows in place of the send bar (ComposeSheet asks it). */
  asking?: boolean;
  onKeep?: () => void;
  onDiscard?: () => void;
  /** The field lost the focus (a card closes itself when it is then empty). */
  onFieldBlur?: () => void;
  handle?: Ref<ComposerHandle>;
}

/**
 * One composer for posts, replies and quotes, with up to four images (UI design, section 6.15), on its parts: the field,
 * the image tray, the quoted post's preview (no live link in it), and the send bar with the ring and the Post button, or,
 * while a sheet asks, the discard question. composer/state.ts holds what is being written and says what follows; the
 * text is kept on the device per context (lib/drafts.ts) from the first keystroke, 500 ms after typing stops, and the
 * draft is removed when the post is sent or discarded. Sending fires the success haptic and the toast with View, and
 * hands the post on; the field keeps or gets back the focus as its container decides. States reach assistive
 * technology through aria-* props: react-native-web 0.21 ignores accessibilityState.
 *
 * 2d (4.5, 10.3, 10.6): while the text names a handle (MENTION_TOKEN), a line under the field says that up to 10 named
 * accounts are told, their settings permitting; no account is looked up while typing (decision 13). One option sits above
 * the send bar, "Hide like and repost counts", off for every new post, sent as hideCounts.
 */
export function Composer({ replyTo, quoteOf, onPosted, onCancel, autoFocus, onDirtyChange, asking = false, onKeep, onDiscard, onFieldBlur, handle }: ComposerProps) {
  const { state: session } = useSession();
  const account = session.status === "signed-in" ? session.me.user.id : null;
  const context = draftContext(replyTo?.id, quoteOf?.id);
  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(composerReducer, context, (opening) => initialComposer(opening, account ? readDraft(account, opening) : ""));
  const uploads = useImageUploads((images) => dispatch({ type: "images", images }));
  const view = composerView(state);
  const haptic = useHaptics();
  const field = useRef<TextInput>(null);
  const { colors } = useTheme();
  const [hideCounts, setHideCounts] = useState(false);

  // One keeper per account and context; leaving writes what is still waiting.
  const keeper = useRef(createDraftKeeper(account, context));
  useEffect(() => {
    const own = createDraftKeeper(account, context);
    keeper.current = own;
    return () => own.dispose();
  }, [account, context]);

  useEffect(() => {
    onDirtyChange?.(view.hasContent);
  }, [view.hasContent, onDirtyChange]);
  useImperativeHandle(handle, () => ({ focus: () => field.current?.focus() }), []);

  // When the question is withdrawn (Keep writing, or Escape while it asks), the focus goes back to the words.
  const wasAsking = useRef(asking);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (wasAsking.current && !asking) field.current?.focus();
    wasAsking.current = asking;
  }, [asking]);

  const type = (text: string) => {
    dispatch({ type: "type", text });
    keeper.current.typed(text);
  };

  async function submit() {
    if (!view.ready) return;
    dispatch({ type: "send" });
    try {
      const post = await social.createPost({
        body: state.text,
        media: state.images.map((image) => ({ id: image.id!, alt: image.alt })),
        ...(replyTo ? { replyToId: replyTo.id } : {}),
        ...(quoteOf ? { quoteOfId: quoteOf.id } : {}),
        hideCounts,
      });
      // Touch and sight on the same frame: the haptic before the composer empties.
      haptic("success");
      keeper.current.sent();
      uploads.clear();
      dispatch({ type: "sent" });
      setHideCounts(false);
      announceSent(view.kind, post);
      onPosted?.(post);
    } catch (err) {
      dispatch({ type: "failed", error: errorMessage(err) });
    }
  }

  const discard = () => {
    keeper.current.discarded();
    dispatch({ type: "discard" });
    onDiscard?.();
  };

  const addImage = canPickImages && state.images.length < MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST ? () => void pickImages().then(uploads.add) : undefined;

  return (
    <View>
      <ComposerField fieldRef={field} kind={view.kind} value={state.text} onChangeText={type} length={view.length} autoFocus={autoFocus} onBlur={onFieldBlur} />
      {hasMention(state.text) ? (
        <Text variant="meta" tone="medium" className="mt-1">
          {ACTIVITY_WORDS["activity.composer.mentions"]}
        </Text>
      ) : null}
      <ComposerImages images={state.images} onAlt={uploads.setAlt} onRemove={uploads.remove} />
      {quoteOf ? <QuoteEmbed quote={{ ...quoteOf, quoteOf: null }} preview /> : null}
      {uploads.notice ? (
        <Text accessibilityRole="alert" variant="meta" tone="danger" className="mt-2">
          {uploads.notice}
        </Text>
      ) : null}
      {state.error ? (
        <Text accessibilityRole="alert" tone="danger" className="mt-2">
          {state.error}
        </Text>
      ) : null}
      {asking ? null : (
        // The kit's switch row: the switch is the one control, and the row around it, 52 px tall, is its pointer target.
        <View className="mt-2 border-t border-line-low">
          <ListRow
            label={UI_WORDS["post.hideCounts.option"]}
            control={{
              kind: "switch",
              value: hideCounts,
              onValueChange: setHideCounts,
              element: <Switch accessibilityLabel={UI_WORDS["post.hideCounts.option"]} value={hideCounts} onValueChange={setHideCounts} {...switchColours(colors)} />,
            }}
          />
        </View>
      )}
      {asking ? (
        <DiscardDialog onDiscard={discard} onKeep={() => onKeep?.()} />
      ) : (
        <SendBar onAddImage={addImage} length={view.length} onCancel={onCancel} label={view.button} ready={view.ready} busy={state.busy} onPost={() => void submit()} />
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { useEffect, useImperativeHandle, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type ReactElement, type Ref } from "react";
import { AppState, Platform, View } from "react-native";
import Animated, { FadeIn } from "react-native-reanimated";
import type { PostView, TimelineItem } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { List, useStable, type ListHandle } from "@/components/list/List";
import { errorMessage } from "@/lib/api";
import { useAppearance } from "@/lib/appearance";
import { onPosted, readFeedCache, writeFeedCache, type FeedSnapshot } from "@/lib/feed-cache";
import { feedRows, timelineTime, trimOlder, type FeedName, type FeedRow } from "@/lib/feed-rows";
import { useMotion } from "@/lib/motion";
import { createNewPosts, gapRows, NEW_LIMIT, newRows, pageVisible, pollActive, type NewPostsClock } from "@/lib/new-posts";
import { createPlaceKeeper, openingRow, readPlace, type Place, type PlaceKeeper, type PlaceRow } from "@/lib/reading-place";
import { useShellScroll } from "@/lib/shell-scroll";
import { social, type Page } from "@/lib/social";
import { UI_WORDS } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { GettingStarted } from "@/components/activity/GettingStarted";
import { FeedRowView, feedRowVersion, type PostPlace } from "./FeedRows";
import { NewPostsPill } from "./NewPostsPill";
import { timelineKey } from "./PagedList";
import { PostCard } from "./PostCard";

/**
 * Home's Following and Latest (UI design, sections 7.5 and 8.2; decisions 6 to 9): a feed that keeps the reader's place.
 *
 * - It opens where the reader stopped (lib/reading-place.ts) when that post is among the newest 100: page one is read
 *   with limit=50, and a second page of 50 when the place is not in the first, before anything shows; otherwise, or with
 *   "Open feeds at the newest post", it opens at the newest. The marker sits above the first post the reader had already
 *   seen, and the pill counts the posts above the place that are newer than that.
 * - A tab change keeps it mounted (Home keys it by the reader only): the feed it leaves is kept for the session with its
 *   rows, cursor and place (lib/feed-cache.ts), and the feed it opens comes back from there without asking page one again.
 * - New posts are asked for 30 s after it opens and every 60 s, only while Home is focused and the page visible
 *   (lib/new-posts.ts); they are put above the reader's row, which does not move, and the pill counts them until they
 *   have come into view. All 50 new gives the gap row, which reads the rest on demand.
 * - The reader's own new post goes on top; at the top of the feed it fades in and pushes the rows down (new-own-post).
 * - Load more stays at the end of each page; with "Load older posts automatically" the next page loads two screens
 *   before the end, but not below the marker. Past 300 rows the oldest pages go and come back through Load more.
 *
 * A signed-out reader gets none of the place, the marker, the pill or the asking: Latest as it is, with Load more.
 */

export interface FeedListHandle {
  /** The reader's own new post, on top of this feed. */
  posted(post: PostView): void;
}

/** Home's feeds read 50 posts a page, the most Pagination allows, so the place is found in two pages (decision 9). */
const FEED_LIMIT = 50;

const fetchFeed = (feed: FeedName, cursor?: string, limit = FEED_LIMIT): Promise<Page<TimelineItem>> => (feed === "following" ? social.following(cursor, limit) : social.latest(cursor, limit));

const placeRow = (item: TimelineItem): PlaceRow => ({ key: timelineKey(item), time: timelineTime(item) });

interface FeedState {
  feed: FeedName;
  items: TimelineItem[];
  cursor: string | null;
  ends: [string, string | null][];
  status: "loading" | "ready" | "error";
  error: string | null;
  loadingMore: boolean;
  moreError: string | null;
  gap: { after: string; cursor: string } | null;
  gapBusy: boolean;
  /** The newest post the reader had seen when the feed opened: the marker's place. */
  marker: PlaceRow | null;
  caughtUp: boolean;
  /** New posts above the reader that have not come into view yet: the pill's count. */
  unread: string[];
}

const loading = (feed: FeedName): FeedState => ({
  feed,
  items: [],
  cursor: null,
  ends: [],
  status: "loading",
  error: null,
  loadingMore: false,
  moreError: null,
  gap: null,
  gapBusy: false,
  marker: null,
  caughtUp: false,
  unread: [],
});

/** The last row of a page, with the cursor its page gave: where the oldest rows can be cut and read again. */
const pageEnd = (page: Page<TimelineItem>): [string, string | null][] => (page.items.length > 0 ? [[timelineKey(page.items.at(-1)!), page.nextCursor]] : []);

/** The index of the first post at or below a row of the list: the post the reader sees at the top. */
function postAt(rows: readonly FeedRow<TimelineItem>[], items: readonly TimelineItem[], key: string | null): number {
  const at = key === null ? -1 : rows.findIndex((row) => row.key === key);
  if (at < 0) return -1;
  const post = rows.slice(at).find((row) => row.kind === "post");
  return post ? items.findIndex((item) => timelineKey(item) === post.key) : items.length;
}

export function FeedList({
  feed,
  reader,
  active,
  header,
  onShowLatest,
  handle,
}: {
  feed: FeedName;
  /** The signed-in account's id, or null signed out. */
  reader: string | null;
  /** Home has the focus (a screen above it does not cover it). */
  active: boolean;
  header?: ReactElement;
  onShowLatest: () => void;
  handle?: Ref<FeedListHandle>;
}) {
  const appearance = useAppearance();
  const motion = useMotion();
  const scroll = useShellScroll();
  const [state, setState] = useState<FeedState>(() => loading(feed));
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(pageVisible);
  const list = useRef<ListHandle>(null);
  const sequence = useRef(0);
  const keeper = useRef<PlaceKeeper | null>(null);
  const clock = useRef<NewPostsClock | null>(null);
  const pendingHold = useRef<{ key: string; offset: number } | null>(null);
  /** The reader's own new post, which fades in where it lands. */
  const own = useRef<string | null>(null);
  // The latest state and settings, for the callbacks that rows and timers keep.
  const latest = useRef({ state, openNewest: appearance.openNewest, rows: [] as FeedRow<TimelineItem>[], top: null as string | null });
  latest.current.state = state;
  latest.current.openNewest = appearance.openNewest;

  /** Page one, and page two when the place is not in page one, then the feed as it opens. */
  const open = useStable(async (place: Place | null, mine: number) => {
    try {
      const first = await fetchFeed(feed);
      if (mine !== sequence.current) return;
      let items = first.items;
      let cursor = first.nextCursor;
      const ends = pageEnd(first);
      const openNewest = latest.current.openNewest;
      let at = openingRow(items.map(placeRow), place, openNewest);
      if (!at && place && !openNewest && cursor !== null && !items.some((item) => timelineKey(item) === place.top.key)) {
        const second = await fetchFeed(feed, cursor);
        if (mine !== sequence.current) return;
        const known = new Set(items.map(timelineKey));
        const both = [...items, ...second.items.filter((item) => !known.has(timelineKey(item)))];
        at = openingRow(both.map(placeRow), place, false);
        if (at) {
          items = both;
          cursor = second.nextCursor;
          ends.push(...pageEnd(second));
        }
      }
      const marker = reader && place ? place.newest : null;
      const top = at ? items.findIndex((item) => timelineKey(item) === at) : 0;
      // The posts above the place that are newer than the newest the reader had seen: the pill counts them.
      const unread = marker ? items.slice(0, top).filter((item) => Date.parse(timelineTime(item)) > Date.parse(marker.time)).map(timelineKey) : [];
      pendingHold.current = at ? { key: at, offset: 0 } : null;
      setState({ ...loading(feed), items, cursor, ends, status: "ready", marker, unread });
    } catch (err) {
      if (mine === sequence.current) setState({ ...loading(feed), status: "error", error: errorMessage(err) });
    }
  });

  // Opening a feed, at mount and on a tab change: from the session's cache, else from the API. Leaving it keeps it in
  // the cache and writes the place. A layout effect, so the old feed's rows are never painted under the new tab.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const mine = ++sequence.current;
    const place = reader ? readPlace(reader, feed) : null;
    keeper.current = createPlaceKeeper(reader, feed, place);
    // The list stays mounted across tabs: the feed it opens starts at its own top, or at the row it was left at.
    list.current?.toTop(false);
    const kept = readFeedCache(reader, feed);
    if (kept) {
      pendingHold.current = kept.view;
      setState({ ...loading(feed), items: kept.items, cursor: kept.cursor, ends: kept.ends, gap: kept.gap, marker: kept.marker, unread: kept.unread, status: "ready" });
    } else {
      setState(loading(feed));
      void open(place, mine);
    }
    return () => {
      sequence.current++;
      const left = latest.current.state;
      if (left.feed === feed && left.status === "ready") {
        const snapshot: FeedSnapshot = { items: left.items, cursor: left.cursor, ends: left.ends, gap: left.gap, marker: left.marker, unread: left.unread, view: list.current?.view() ?? null };
        writeFeedCache(reader, feed, snapshot);
      }
      keeper.current?.hidden();
      keeper.current?.dispose();
      keeper.current = null;
    };
  }, [feed, reader]);

  const result = feedRows({
    items: state.items,
    keyOf: timelineKey,
    timeOf: timelineTime,
    status: state.feed === feed ? state.status : "loading",
    error: state.error,
    cursor: state.cursor,
    loadingMore: state.loadingMore,
    moreError: state.moreError,
    marker: state.marker ? { time: state.marker.time, caughtUp: state.caughtUp } : null,
    gap: state.gap ? { after: state.gap.after, busy: state.gapBusy } : null,
    feed,
    autoLoad: appearance.autoLoad,
  });
  latest.current.rows = result.rows;

  // Once the rows are drawn, the list shows the place (or the row a tab left at); with the marker right above the place,
  // the marker, so "You were here" is the first thing the reader sees.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const hold = pendingHold.current;
    if (!hold || state.status !== "ready") return;
    pendingHold.current = null;
    const at = result.rows.findIndex((row) => row.key === hold.key);
    const key = hold.offset === 0 && at > 0 && result.rows[at - 1]!.kind === "marker" ? "marker" : hold.key;
    list.current?.hold(key, hold.offset);
  }, [state]);

  // The page hidden: the place is written now, and nothing is asked until it is visible again.
  useEffect(() => {
    const change = (shown: boolean) => {
      setVisible(shown);
      if (!shown) keeper.current?.hidden();
    };
    if (Platform.OS === "web" && typeof document !== "undefined") {
      const onVisibility = () => change(pageVisible());
      const onHide = () => keeper.current?.hidden();
      document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", onVisibility);
      window.addEventListener("pagehide", onHide);
      return () => {
        document.removeEventListener("visibilitychange", onVisibility);
        window.removeEventListener("pagehide", onHide);
      };
    }
    const subscription = AppState.addEventListener("change", (next) => change(next === "active"));
    return () => subscription.remove();
  }, []);

  /** Rows put above the reader's: from a poll they are unread and keep the reader's row in place. */
  const insertAbove = (added: TimelineItem[], gapCursor: string | null, unread: boolean) => {
    setState((current) => {
      const keys = added.map(timelineKey);
      let items = [...added, ...current.items];
      let cursor = current.cursor;
      let ends = current.ends;
      const trimmed = trimOlder(items, timelineKey, new Map(ends));
      if (trimmed) {
        items = trimmed.items;
        cursor = trimmed.cursor;
        const kept = new Set(items.map(timelineKey));
        ends = ends.filter(([key]) => kept.has(key));
      }
      return {
        ...current,
        items,
        cursor,
        ends,
        unread: unread ? [...keys, ...current.unread] : current.unread,
        caughtUp: unread ? false : current.caughtUp,
        gap: gapCursor && keys.length > 0 ? { after: keys.at(-1)!, cursor: gapCursor } : current.gap,
      };
    });
  };

  /** The poll: page one of 50, and the posts above the first one listed. */
  const ask = useStable(async () => {
    const asked = latest.current.state;
    if (asked.status !== "ready" || asked.feed !== feed) return;
    const page = await fetchFeed(feed, undefined, NEW_LIMIT);
    const now = latest.current.state;
    if (now.status !== "ready" || now.feed !== feed) return;
    const { added, gapCursor } = newRows(page, timelineKey, new Set(now.items.map(timelineKey)));
    if (added.length === 0) return;
    // Nothing the reader reads moves: the row at the top stays where it is, even at the very top.
    list.current?.keepNext();
    insertAbove(added, gapCursor, true);
  });

  // The clock runs per feed for an account, and only while Home is focused, the page visible and the feed in.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!reader) return undefined;
    const made = createNewPosts(ask);
    clock.current = made;
    return () => {
      made.dispose();
      clock.current = null;
    };
  }, [feed, reader]);
  useEffect(() => {
    clock.current?.setActive(pollActive({ focused: active, signedIn: reader !== null, selected: true, visible }) && state.status === "ready");
  }, [active, visible, state.status, feed, reader]);

  const more = useStable(async () => {
    const current = latest.current.state;
    if (current.loadingMore || current.cursor === null) return;
    const mine = sequence.current;
    setState((now) => ({ ...now, loadingMore: true, moreError: null }));
    try {
      const page = await fetchFeed(feed, current.cursor);
      if (mine !== sequence.current) return;
      setState((now) => {
        const known = new Set(now.items.map(timelineKey));
        return { ...now, items: [...now.items, ...page.items.filter((item) => !known.has(timelineKey(item)))], cursor: page.nextCursor, ends: [...now.ends, ...pageEnd(page)], loadingMore: false };
      });
    } catch (err) {
      if (mine === sequence.current) setState((now) => ({ ...now, loadingMore: false, moreError: errorMessage(err) }));
    }
  });

  const fillGap = useStable(async () => {
    const current = latest.current.state;
    if (!current.gap || current.gapBusy) return;
    const mine = sequence.current;
    setState((now) => ({ ...now, gapBusy: true }));
    try {
      const page = await fetchFeed(feed, current.gap.cursor, NEW_LIMIT);
      if (mine !== sequence.current) return;
      setState((now) => {
        if (!now.gap) return { ...now, gapBusy: false };
        const { added, gapCursor } = gapRows(page, timelineKey, new Set(now.items.map(timelineKey)));
        const at = now.items.findIndex((item) => timelineKey(item) === now.gap!.after) + 1;
        const items = [...now.items.slice(0, at), ...added, ...now.items.slice(at)];
        return { ...now, items, gapBusy: false, gap: gapCursor && added.length > 0 ? { after: timelineKey(added.at(-1)!), cursor: gapCursor } : null };
      });
    } catch {
      // The gap stays, to be pressed again.
      if (mine === sequence.current) setState((now) => ({ ...now, gapBusy: false }));
    }
  });

  const retry = useStable(() => {
    const mine = ++sequence.current;
    setState(loading(feed));
    void open(reader ? readPlace(reader, feed) : null, mine);
  });

  const remove = useStable((key: string) => setState((now) => ({ ...now, items: now.items.filter((item) => timelineKey(item) !== key), unread: now.unread.filter((unread) => unread !== key) })));

  // The row at the top: the place's top, and the unread posts that have come into view leave the pill's count.
  const onTop = useStable((key: string | null) => {
    latest.current.top = key;
    const now = latest.current.state;
    const index = postAt(latest.current.rows, now.items, key);
    if (index >= 0 && index < now.items.length) keeper.current?.top(placeRow(now.items[index]!));
    if (index < 0 || now.unread.length === 0) return;
    const above = new Set(now.items.slice(0, index).map(timelineKey));
    const unread = now.unread.filter((unreadKey) => above.has(unreadKey));
    if (unread.length === now.unread.length) return;
    setState((current) => ({ ...current, unread, caughtUp: current.caughtUp || unread.length === 0 }));
  });

  // Rows half in view for half a second: the place's newest. The marker reached from above, with nothing unread above it,
  // says the reader is caught up.
  const onViewed = useStable((keys: string[]) => {
    const now = latest.current.state;
    const byKey = new Map(now.items.map((item) => [timelineKey(item), item]));
    keeper.current?.seen(keys.flatMap((key) => (byKey.has(key) ? [placeRow(byKey.get(key)!)] : [])));
    if (!keys.includes("marker") || now.caughtUp || now.unread.length > 0) return;
    const rows = latest.current.rows;
    const top = rows.findIndex((row) => row.key === latest.current.top);
    if (top >= 0 && top < rows.findIndex((row) => row.key === "marker")) setState((current) => ({ ...current, caughtUp: true }));
  });

  const scrolled = useStable(() => keeper.current?.scrolled());

  // The pill: to the oldest unread new post, the first one above the reader's place, so they read on upwards in order.
  const jump = useStable(() => {
    const now = latest.current.state;
    const unread = new Set(now.unread);
    const oldest = [...now.items].reverse().find((item) => unread.has(timelineKey(item)));
    if (oldest) list.current?.jumpTo(timelineKey(oldest), !motion.reduced);
  });

  // The reader's own new post on top. Home tells it, and so does lib/feed-cache.ts for a post sent from any screen; the
  // second word of the same post is passed over (own.current is set at once, before the state that holds it renders).
  const posted = useStable((post: PostView) => {
    const now = latest.current.state;
    if (own.current === post.id || now.status !== "ready" || now.items.some((item) => timelineKey(item) === post.id)) return;
    own.current = post.id;
    insertAbove([{ kind: "post", post }], null, false);
  });
  useImperativeHandle(handle, () => ({ posted }), [posted]);
  useEffect(() => onPosted((who, post) => (who === reader ? posted(post) : undefined)), [reader, posted]);

  const renderPost = (item: TimelineItem, place: PostPlace, key: string) => {
    const card = <PostCard post={item.post} repostedBy={item.kind === "repost" ? item.repostedBy : undefined} onDeleted={() => remove(key)} {...place} />;
    // The reader's own new post fades in where it lands (new-own-post, 220 ms; at once under reduced motion).
    return key === own.current && !motion.reduced ? <Animated.View entering={FadeIn.duration(220)}>{card}</Animated.View> : card;
  };
  // 2d (decision 25, 10.7): an account's empty Following is the Getting started panel, which goes once Following has a post.
  const empty = feed === "following" ? <GettingStarted onShowLatest={onShowLatest} /> : { title: UI_WORDS["feed.empty.latest.title"], body: UI_WORDS["feed.empty.latest.body"] };

  return (
    <View className="flex-1">
      <List
        handle={list}
        rows={result.rows}
        keyOf={(row) => row.key}
        versionOf={(row) => feedRowVersion(row, result.setSize)}
        renderRow={(row, index) => <FeedRowView row={row} index={index} setSize={result.setSize} renderPost={renderPost} empty={empty} onRetry={retry} onLoadMore={more} onGap={fillGap} />}
        header={header}
        feed
        label={feed === "following" ? UI_WORDS["home.following"] : UI_WORDS["home.latest"]}
        busy={state.status === "loading" || state.loadingMore || state.gapBusy}
        autoLoad={result.autoLoad}
        onEndReached={more}
        onViewed={onViewed}
        onTop={onTop}
        onScrolled={scrolled}
        // Pull to refresh on a phone asks for new posts now; they push the rows down, since the reader is at the top.
        refreshing={false}
        onRefresh={Platform.OS === "web" ? undefined : () => void ask()}
      />
      {reader ? <NewPostsPill count={state.unread.length} more={state.gap !== null} top={scroll.headerSpace} headerY={scroll.headerY} onPress={jump} /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, View } from "react-native";
import Animated, { runOnJS, useAnimatedStyle, useSharedValue, withTiming, type SharedValue } from "react-native-reanimated";
import { Icon } from "@/components/kit/Icon";
import { FOCUS_RING, dataAttribute, pressDelay } from "@/components/kit/interaction";
import { Text } from "@/components/kit/Text";
import { VisuallyHidden } from "@/components/kit/VisuallyHidden";
import { useMotion } from "@/lib/motion";
import { UI_WORDS, fill } from "@/lib/ui-words";
import { cn } from "@/theme/cn";
import { CaughtUpCheck } from "./FeedRows";

/**
 * "N new posts above" (UI design, decision 7, sections 5.2, 8.2 and 10): the one sign that new posts arrived, floating
 * 12 px under the header, centred, in the accent fill with the newer icon. Its name adds "above, go to the first one";
 * pressing it scrolls to the oldest unread new post, the first one above the reader's place, so the reader reads on
 * upwards in time order. The count falls as rows come into view; at zero it says "You're all caught up" for two seconds
 * (opacity only) and leaves. It comes in from 8 px above and leaves by fading (pill-show: 200 ms in, 150 ms out; reduced,
 * opacity only), and a screen reader hears "N new posts above" once, when it first shows, never on later counts. Like
 * every floating layer it keeps a border in forced colours (section 4.6). 2d (10.2): Activity's pill is this one with its
 * own words passed in, "1 new", "{n} new" or "20+ new" (`wordsFor`), and its name's template (`label`).
 */

/** How long "You're all caught up" stays once the count reaches zero. */
export const CAUGHT_UP_MS = 2000;

/** The pill's words for a count: "1 new post", "N new posts", or "50+ new posts" when a gap holds more not yet read. */
export function pillWords(count: number, more = false): string {
  if (more || count > 50) return UI_WORDS["feed.pill.many"];
  if (count === 1) return UI_WORDS["feed.pill.one"];
  return fill(UI_WORDS["feed.pill"], { n: count });
}

export function NewPostsPill({
  count,
  more = false,
  top,
  headerY,
  onPress,
  wordsFor = pillWords,
  label = UI_WORDS["feed.pill.label"],
}: {
  count: number;
  more?: boolean;
  /** The room the phone's floating header takes; the pill sits 12 px under it. */
  top: number;
  /** The header's slide on a phone: the pill moves up with it when it hides. */
  headerY?: SharedValue<number>;
  onPress: () => void;
  wordsFor?: (count: number, more: boolean) => string;
  label?: string;
}) {
  const motion = useMotion();
  // What shows: the count, "You're all caught up" for two seconds after it reached zero, or nothing.
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<"hidden" | "count" | "caughtUp">(count > 0 ? "count" : "hidden");
  const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(count > 0);
  const [announced, setAnnounced] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const had = useRef(count > 0);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (count > 0) {
      if (!had.current) setAnnounced(fill(UI_WORDS["feed.pill.announce"], { visible: wordsFor(count, more) }));
      had.current = true;
      setPhase("count");
      setMounted(true);
      return undefined;
    }
    if (!had.current) return undefined;
    had.current = false;
    setPhase("caughtUp");
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setPhase("hidden"), CAUGHT_UP_MS);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [count > 0, count]);

  const shown = useSharedValue(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    const target = phase === "hidden" ? 0 : 1;
    if (shown.value === target) {
      if (target === 0) setMounted(false);
      return;
    }
    shown.value = withTiming(target, motion.timing("easeOut", target === 1 ? 200 : 150), (finished) => {
      "worklet";
      if (finished && target === 0) runOnJS(setMounted)(false);
    });
  }, [phase, mounted]);
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    opacity: shown.value,
    transform: [{ translateY: (headerY ? headerY.value : 0) + (motion.reduced ? 0 : (1 - shown.value) * -8) }],
  }));

  // While it fades out the pill keeps the words it last showed.
  const shownWords = useRef("");
  if (phase === "caughtUp") shownWords.current = UI_WORDS["feed.caughtUp"];
  else if (phase === "count" && count > 0) shownWords.current = wordsFor(count, more);
  const words = shownWords.current;
  return (
    <>
      {/* Heard once, when the pill first shows. */}
      <VisuallyHidden role="status">{announced ?? ""}</VisuallyHidden>
      {mounted ? (
        <View pointerEvents="box-none" className="absolute left-0 right-0 z-20 items-center" style={{ top: top + 12 }}>
          <Animated.View style={style}>
            <Pressable
              {...dataAttribute("pill")}
              accessibilityRole="button"
              aria-label={phase === "caughtUp" ? words : fill(label, { visible: words })}
              disabled={phase !== "count"}
              onPress={onPress}
              {...pressDelay(0)}
              className={cn(
                "min-h-[44px] flex-row items-center gap-2 rounded-full border border-accent bg-accent px-4 active:opacity-90 web:forced-colors:border-[color:CanvasText]",
                FOCUS_RING,
              )}
            >
              {phase === "caughtUp" ? <CaughtUpCheck tone="on-accent" /> : <Icon name="newer" size={20} tone="on-accent" />}
              <Text variant="body-strong" tone="on-accent">
                {words}
              </Text>
            </Pressable>
          </Animated.View>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}
```
